Title: Create the users table and register an account in one request
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/register with {"email":" Ada@Example.com ","password":"correct horse battery"} returns 201, sets a fr_session cookie, and returns {"user_id","email":"Ada@Example.com","role":"customer"} with the email trimmed and its case as entered; SELECT email, role, password_version, last_signed_in_at FROM users WHERE lower(email)='ada@example.com' returns exactly 1 row with role='customer', password_version=1 and last_signed_in_at IS NULL; SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name='users' returns exactly id, email, password_hash, role, password_version, created_at, last_signed_in_at and nothing else; password_hash is not equal to the submitted password, and the literal string "correct horse battery" is absent from the 201 response body, from the stdout captured for the whole request with the log level set to DEBUG, and from SELECT users::text FROM users WHERE lower(email)='ada@example.com'; a second POST with "ADA@example.com" returns 409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED with the body "An account already exists for that email address. Sign in instead, or reset the password if you have forgotten it."; 20 simultaneous identical registrations -- run with RATE_LIMIT_REGISTER_IP_PER_HOUR configured above 20 for that run, which per P-XCT-07 sets a bucket size and does not disable a control, every request still being counted, bucketed and refusable -- report exactly 1 success and 19 conflicts, SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE lower(email)='ada@example.com' returns 1, no response carries error.code RATE_LIMITED, and no response is a 500; role is never read from the request body -- a request carrying "role":"admin" still produces a row with role='customer'
SourceRef: P-ACC-01 EP-ACC-01 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-052 SRC-001 §5.4.1 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-02

Title: Enforce the password rules and hash off the event loop, with one verification on every branch
AcceptanceCriteria: With PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH=12: an 11-character password on register or reset-confirm returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with "Your password must be at least 12 characters. It does not have to contain numbers or symbols."; the Devanagari string of 28 code points encoding to 84 UTF-8 bytes returns 422 with details.byte_length=84 and the message quoting 84, not an example value; "correct horse battery" (21 bytes) and " leading space kept " are both accepted and the password is never trimmed, so signing in without the spaces fails; no composition rule is applied -- a 12-character all-lowercase password is accepted; setting PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH=14 makes the same 12-character request return "at least 14 characters", proving the figure is interpolated and not a literal, while 72 stays a literal because it is bcrypt truncation and has no variable behind it; bcrypt runs off the event loop, asserted structurally rather than by timing: the hash function is wrapped for the test so that it records the boolean threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread() at the moment it is entered, the request is served by the async handler on the main thread, and the recorded boolean is False; with a counter wrapping the verify function, POST /api/auth/login increments it by exactly 1 for an unregistered address and by exactly 1 for a registered address with a wrong password, both returning 401 CREDENTIALS_INVALID -- and by exactly 1 for an account whose password_hash is the unusable sentinel, so there is no third branch and no early return; no assertion in this story measures elapsed time, asserted by rg -n 'time\.time|time\.monotonic|time\.perf_counter|datetime\.now|datetime\.utcnow|sleep\(' over this story's test module returning 0 hits; SELECT is_nullable FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name='users' AND column_name='password_hash' returns NO, and SELECT count(*) - count(DISTINCT password_hash) FROM users WHERE last_signed_in_at IS NULL returns 0, so no two no-password accounts share one sentinel value
StatusNote: Every clause is asserted, including the 11-character reset-confirm half now that EP-ACC-06 exists.
SourceRef: P-ACC-03 EP-ACC-01 EP-ACC-02 FR-ADR-050 SRC-001 §7.4 SRC-002 §5.4.1

Title: Sign in, record the sign-in instant, and answer identically for an unknown address
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/login with the registered address in any case and the correct password returns 200, sets fr_session, and returns {"user_id","email","role"}; SELECT last_signed_in_at FROM users WHERE id=:id equals the injected clock instant, and no other column of that row changes -- SELECT email, password_hash, role, password_version, created_at FROM users WHERE id=:id returns byte-identical values before and after the sign-in; SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE actor_user_id=:id returns 0 -- signing in is not a privileged write and writes no audit row; an unknown address and a registered address with the wrong password both return 401 CREDENTIALS_INVALID, and their bodies are byte-identical once error.request_id is removed from each -- the error envelope in docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json carries request_id on every error and it is unique per request, so it is the one field that must differ and the only field exempted from the comparison; both carry error.code CREDENTIALS_INVALID and error.message "That email address and password do not match an account.", both carry the same Content-Type, and neither body holds a key the other does not, so nothing but the request id separates the two answers; and after both attempts SELECT last_signed_in_at FROM users WHERE id=:id is unchanged; a missing or empty field returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED "Enter your email address and password."; an account whose stored password is 10 characters still signs in with 200, because sign-in never length-validates the password; 9 consecutive failed attempts -- one short of the per-email bucket capacity of 10 that S-ACC-09 sets, so the limiter never fires in this run -- produce 9 x 401 and never a locked or disabled account: SELECT role FROM users WHERE id=:id is unchanged, SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name='users' still returns exactly the seven columns S-ACC-01 names and so contains no locked, locked_until, disabled, failed_attempts or lockout_expires_at column, and the 10th attempt with the correct password returns 200
SourceRef: P-ACC-02 EP-ACC-02 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-018 SRC-001 §5.4.1 SRC-002 §4.8

Title: Issue the session cookie, revoke it on a password change, and keep sign-out public
AcceptanceCriteria: The Set-Cookie from a successful sign-in is fr_session=<jwt>; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=43200, with the Secure attribute present when COOKIE_SECURE=true and absent when COOKIE_SECURE=false; the process refuses to start when COOKIE_SECURE or JWT_SECRET is unset -- neither has a default, a startup with COOKIE_SECURE unset exits non-zero with the literal "COOKIE_SECURE" present in its captured stderr, and a startup with JWT_SECRET unset exits non-zero with the literal "JWT_SECRET" present in its captured stderr; decoding the JWT payload yields exactly the claims sub, role, pv, iat, exp and no email address and no name; the authorisation dependency reads the users row by primary key on every authenticated request, so a token whose pv is one behind users.password_version returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED "Your session has ended because the password was changed. Sign in to continue.", a token whose users row has been removed returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED "Sign in to continue.", and five further tokens, each re-signed with exactly one of sub, role, pv, iat and exp removed, each return 401 AUTH_REQUIRED rather than the missing claim being read as a default -- five separate assertions, one per claim; a role changed directly in the database takes effect on the very next request rather than at the next sign-in; POST /api/auth/logout returns 204 with Set-Cookie: fr_session=; Max-Age=0 carrying the same attributes the cookie was issued with, and returns 204 with no cookie sent, with an expired cookie, with a malformed cookie and on a second consecutive call -- it is declared auth: public in EP-ACC-03 and S3.8's generated route inventory lists it under "Public -- no session required", so no build may make it 401; SELECT to_regclass('session') returns null -- no session table exists
SourceRef: P-ACC-05 EP-ACC-02 EP-ACC-03 EP-ACC-04 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-053 FR-ADR-069 SRC-002 §7.3 SRC-003 OPEN-TLS-01

Title: Fix the session lifetime at a single configured value and build no refresh token
AcceptanceCriteria: With SESSION_TTL_SECONDS=43200 and the clock injected at 2026-08-14T10:00:00Z, the issued token carries iat=2026-08-14T10:00:00Z and exp=2026-08-14T22:00:00Z and the cookie carries Max-Age=43200, so the cookie and the token cannot outlive each other; with the clock advanced to 2026-08-14T21:59:00Z, GET /api/auth/me returns 200; with the clock advanced to 2026-08-14T22:00:01Z the same request returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED "Your session has ended. Sign in to continue."; every comparison is against the injected clock -- expiry is the application's own comparison of the exp claim against that clock, with the JWT library's built-in expiry verification switched off, so nothing outside the application decides whether a session has ended; no test in this story sleeps or reads the wall clock, asserted by rg -n 'time\.time|time\.monotonic|time\.perf_counter|datetime\.now|datetime\.utcnow|sleep\(' over this story's test module returning 0 hits, and a build that compares against the container clock fails when the container clock is offset from the injected one; SESSION_TTL_SECONDS=0 and a non-integer value each fail startup validation with the variable name present in captured stderr; no refresh, renew or token-exchange route exists, asserted by a route-table walk: no path in docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json and no path in the running app's route table contains the substring refresh, renew, reissue, exchange or session, and the only three paths containing the substring token are EP-HLD-02, EP-HLD-03 and EP-HLD-04 whose path parameter is {hold_token}; the lifetime figure 43200 appears in exactly one place in the codebase -- rg -n '43200' backend/app frontend/src --glob '!**/config*.py' returns 0 hits and rg -n '43200' backend/app/core/config.py returns exactly 1 hit
SourceRef: P-ACC-06 EP-ACC-02 EP-ACC-04 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-053 FR-ADR-018 SRC-002 §7.3

Title: Prove the absence of a verification gate and of any address-change endpoint
AcceptanceCriteria: Immediately after a 201 from POST /api/auth/register the same session reaches every authenticated route with no intermediate step: GET /api/auth/me returns 200 with role "customer", and the JSON object it returns has exactly the keys user_id, email and role -- no key named verified, email_verified, verification_status, confirmed_at or pending; the registration writes nothing to the queue -- SELECT count(*) FROM outbox_message is identical before and after the request, so neither a verification message nor a welcome message is enqueued; no route updates an account's email address, asserted against the route table and the request schemas and not by inspection: walking all 61 endpoints of S3.8's generated route inventory and reading each operation's request-body schema from the running app's OpenAPI document, the set of operations declaring a body property named "email" is exactly {POST /api/auth/register, POST /api/auth/login, POST /api/auth/password-reset/request, POST /api/admin/managers, POST /api/admin/admin-grants} -- five POSTs: four insert a users row or authenticate against one, the fifth (EP-ADM-31) (SRC-008 ROLE-1 and its ADDENDUM, S-ADM-30) inserts an admin_grant row naming an address and writes no users.email, and none of the five addresses an existing users row's email -- and no PATCH and no PUT anywhere in the table declares a body property named "email"; the test fails if that set gains a sixth member or if any PATCH or PUT appears with one; users.email is written once and never again, asserted at the engine: a SQLAlchemy Core before_cursor_execute listener registered for the duration of the module records the SET column names of every UPDATE issued against users, the suite drives register, login, logout, password-reset request, password-reset confirm, POST /api/admin/managers and PUT /api/admin/managers/{user_id}/screens, and the recorded set of changed attribute names is exactly {last_signed_in_at, password_hash, password_version} with "email" never in it; a customer who registers a second account at a different address does not move their first booking -- SELECT user_id FROM booking WHERE reference=:ref is unchanged and equals the first account id; none of the literal strings "verify", "verified", "unverified", "verification", "confirm your email" and "not confirmed" appears, compared case-insensitively, in any of five captured response bodies -- the 201 from register, the 200 from GET /api/auth/me, the 409 from a duplicate register, the 401 from a failed login and the 202 from a password-reset request -- and rg -in 'unverified|not verified|verify your email|verify your address|email_verified' backend/app frontend/src returns 0 hits
SourceRef: P-ACC-04 EP-ACC-01 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-048 FR-ADR-012 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-02 SRC-003 OPEN-EMAIL-01

Title: Send a single-use password reset link and answer identically for an unknown address
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/password-reset/request returns 202 for a registered and for an unregistered address with byte-identical bodies containing "If that email address has an account, a reset link is on its way to it. The link works once and expires in 30 minutes."; the 30 is rendered from PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS / 60 as a whole number of minutes, so with PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS=600 the same string reads "10 minutes" on the 202 body, on SCR-ACC-02's confirmation panel and in the rendered email template, all three asserted in the same run against the same configuration change; for a registered address SELECT count(*) FROM password_reset_token WHERE user_id=:id AND used_at IS NULL returns exactly 1 after two consecutive requests, the earlier row having been marked used, so at most one live token exists per account; the stored row carries token_sha256 equal to the SHA-256 hex of the 43-character token, and the token's own 43 characters appear in none of: SELECT password_reset_token::text FROM password_reset_token WHERE user_id=:id, the 202 response body, and the stdout captured for the whole request with the log level set to DEBUG; expires_at = created_at + 1800 seconds from the injected clock, so a token created at 10:00:00Z has expires_at 10:30:00Z; the token row and one outbox_message row with topic 'password_reset.send' are written in the same transaction -- forcing the transaction to roll back leaves neither row and the queue stub records 0 sends -- and that row has the payload key set exactly message_version, request_id, reset_token_id, user_id, and SELECT payload::text FROM outbox_message WHERE topic='password_reset.send' does not contain the 43-character token (SRC-004 R-3: no database column holds the plaintext); after the commit and before the 202, with the outbox relay stopped, the queue stub records exactly 1 message sent directly by the request, whose body has the key set exactly message_version, request_id, reset_token, reset_token_id, user_id, with reset_token equal to the 43-character token and the SHA-256 hex of reset_token equal to the stored token_sha256 (SRC-004 R-3: the token rides in the queue message only); with that queue send forced to fail the response is still 202 with the byte-identical body, the outbox row still reads status 'pending', and one full outbox relay cycle run afterwards makes the queue stub record 0 messages with topic password_reset.send, so the failed send is not retried (SRC-004 JC-R6-01); for an unregistered address SELECT count(*) FROM password_reset_token is unchanged, no outbox_message row is written and the queue stub records 0 sends; an empty or malformed address returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED "Enter an email address."; the link the confirm screen accepts has the form {PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/account/reset/confirm#token=<the 43-character token>, and the confirm screen reads it from `location.hash` and removes it from the address bar after reading, asserted by the rendered reset email body containing `/account/reset/confirm#token=` and not `?token=`; the process refuses to start when PUBLIC_BASE_URL is unset, exiting non-zero with the literal "PUBLIC_BASE_URL" present in its captured stderr. The rest of what the worker puts in the email is E4 P-TKT-12's and is asserted there, not here
StatusNote: Every backend clause passes. The #token= link form is now the cell's (CR-002 B-1), asserted on the rendered email in tests/tkt/test_s_tkt_15.py. One clause is still open: the "10 minutes" on the 202 body, on SCR-ACC-02's confirmation panel and in the email, all three in the same run. The panel is checked only by seed-rendering in reset.test.mjs, and that run needs a real browser after a submit. The 2026-11-07 screenshots do not show it.
SourceRef: P-ACC-07 EP-ACC-05 SCR-ACC-06 FR-ADR-031 FR-ADR-053 FR-ADR-012 FR-ADR-060 SRC-001 §5.4.1

Title: Complete a password reset once, and only once, ending every existing session
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/password-reset/confirm with a live 43-character token and a valid new password returns 200 and sets a fresh fr_session; in one transaction password_reset_token.used_at is set, users.password_hash is replaced, users.password_version goes from 1 to 2 and users.last_signed_in_at is written from the injected clock -- forcing that transaction to roll back leaves used_at null, password_hash unchanged and password_version 1, so no half of it is observable on its own; the cookie issued before the reset then returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED on GET /api/auth/me while the new cookie returns 200; the single-use guarantee is the conditional UPDATE password_reset_token SET used_at = :now WHERE id = :id AND used_at IS NULL affecting exactly one row inside the same transaction -- 50 simultaneous submissions of one token, run with RATE_LIMIT_RESET_CONFIRM_IP_PER_HOUR configured above 50 for that run so the per-IP confirm bucket cannot refuse any of them (P-XCT-07: setting a configured bucket size is not disabling a control), report exactly 1 success and 49 x 400 RESET_TOKEN_INVALID "That reset link has already been used. Request a new one." with no response carrying error.code RATE_LIMITED, and SELECT password_version FROM users WHERE id=:id is 2 and not 51; an unknown token returns 400 "That reset link is not valid. Request a new one."; a token past expires_at on the injected clock returns 400 "That reset link has expired. Request a new one."; a token of any length other than 43 returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and reaches no database at all, asserted two ways and neither of them by timing: a SQLAlchemy before_cursor_execute listener installed for the test -- the harness must install it, and this criterion is what requires it -- records zero statements issued during the request, and independently the same 42-character request still returns 422 and not 503 when the application is pointed at a closed database port while Redis stays up; the request-body schema for EP-ACC-06 in the running app's OpenAPI document declares exactly the properties token and password, so no old_password and no current_password field exists, and a request carrying an old_password value that does not match the account's current password still returns 200, proving the old password is neither required nor consulted; no confirmation email is sent -- SELECT count(*) FROM outbox_message is unchanged by a successful reset; the submitted token's 43 characters appear in no line of the stdout captured for the whole request with the log level set to DEBUG
SourceRef: P-ACC-08 EP-ACC-06 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-056 SRC-001 §7.4 SRC-001 §5.4.1

Title: Rate limit every credential endpoint, derive Retry-After from the refill rate, and fail closed
AcceptanceCriteria: With Redis up and the clock injected: the 11th POST /api/auth/login for one lower(email) inside 15 minutes returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After: 90 and "Too many sign-in attempts for that email address. Try again in 90 seconds."; the 31st POST /api/auth/login from one IP inside 15 minutes -- the 31 requests using 31 distinct email addresses, so no per-email bucket reaches its capacity of 10 first and the refusal is the per-IP bucket's -- returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After: 30 and "Too many sign-in attempts from this connection. Try again in 30 seconds."; the 6th POST /api/auth/register from one IP in an hour returns Retry-After: 720 and "Too many accounts have been created from this connection. Try again in 12 minutes."; the 6th reset request from one IP in an hour returns Retry-After: 720 and "Too many reset requests from this connection. Try again in 12 minutes."; the 11th reset confirm from one IP in an hour returns Retry-After: 360 and "Too many attempts from this connection. Try again in 6 minutes."; the confirm bucket is separate from the request bucket -- after 5 requests and 6 confirms in one hour the request bucket is empty and the confirm bucket still admits 4 more calls; every confirm request spends a token including one rejected for a malformed token or a failing password; every Retry-After equals ceil(window_seconds / capacity) computed from the bucket that refused and never a constant, so a caller who empties the sign-in per-email bucket at t=0 and retries at t=30s receives Retry-After: 60 and not 90; the refill is computed against the injected clock and never against anything Redis decides for itself -- the application passes its own instant into the limiter's Lua script as an argument and the script issues no redis.call('TIME'), asserted by the literal TIME appearing nowhere in the script file, and the bucket key's Redis TTL is a garbage-collection backstop rather than the mechanism: with the injected clock advanced 90 seconds past an emptied per-email bucket the next request is admitted while PTTL on that key still returns a positive value, so a build whose window ends only when a Redis key expires fails here; two requests from one peer carrying different forged leftmost X-Forwarded-For values are counted in the same bucket, because the key is the rightmost-but-one entry with exactly one trusted proxy; both buckets on an endpoint must have a token -- exhausting either alone produces the 429; with Redis stopped, POST /api/auth/login returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE "Sign-in is unavailable right now. Browsing still works. Try again shortly." and never 200, and GET /api/movies still returns 200 in the same run
StatusNote: Every clause is asserted, including the reset-request and confirm buckets now that EP-ACC-05/06 exist, and GET /api/movies returning 200 with Redis unreachable. "Redis stopped" is simulated by a closed port on the Redis host, which gives the process the same connection refusal.
SourceRef: P-ACC-14 EP-ACC-01 EP-ACC-02 EP-ACC-05 EP-ACC-06 FR-ADR-058 FR-ADR-028 SRC-002 §8.4.1 SRC-002 §7.9

Title: Bind every booking to one user row with ON DELETE RESTRICT, and red-proof the refusal
AcceptanceCriteria: The phase 2 migration declares booking.user_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT; SELECT confdeltype FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid='booking'::regclass AND contype='f' AND confrelid='users'::regclass returns 'r' -- not 'c' and not 'n'; SELECT is_nullable FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name='booking' AND column_name='user_id' returns NO, which is why SET NULL is not a candidate; with one user row and one booking row referencing it, DELETE FROM users WHERE id=:id raises SQLSTATE 23503 foreign_key_violation, the transaction rolls back, and SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE user_id=:id and SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE id=:id both still return 1; the CASCADE refusal is red-proved rather than asserted -- with the constraint temporarily redefined ON DELETE CASCADE the same DELETE succeeds and leaves SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE user_id=:id at 0 with its booking_seat rows and their snapshotted price_paise gone, then the constraint is restored to RESTRICT and the restore is verified by repeating the first delete and observing 23503 again; deleting a user row that no booking references succeeds, and a live session for that row then returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED "Sign in to continue." from GET /api/auth/me, so P-ACC-05 exception 5 is reachable and is not dead code; the booking owner comes from the authorisation dependency and never from the request, asserted by a route-table walk over all 61 endpoints of S3.8's generated route inventory: exactly one path carries {user_id} (PUT /api/admin/managers/{user_id}/screens, EP-ADM-24, which writes no booking row); no operation whose path begins /api/bookings, /api/me/ or /api/showtimes declares a path parameter, query parameter or request-body property named user_id, owner_id or on_behalf_of; and the inventory's only four DELETE operations are EP-ADM-21 DELETE /api/admin/seats/{seat_id}, EP-ADM-32 DELETE /api/admin/admin-grants/{grant_id} (SRC-008 ROLE-1 and its ADDENDUM, S-ADM-30), EP-HLD-03 DELETE /api/holds/{hold_token}/seats/{seat_id} and EP-HLD-04 DELETE /api/holds/{hold_token}, no one of whose paths carries a {user_id} parameter or begins /api/admin/users, so the table contains no operation that deletes a users row
SourceRef: P-ACC-09 FR-ADR-012 FR-ADR-013 FR-ADR-014 FR-ADR-039 SRC-001 §9.2 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-02

Title: Return the caller's own bookings in two groups, both arrays always present
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/me/bookings with a valid session returns 200 carrying upcoming, past, page, page_size, total_upcoming and total_past, and both arrays are present in every response -- with ?group=upcoming, past is [] and total_past still carries its true count, never omitted; for a caller with total_upcoming=2 and total_past=37 at page_size=20: ?page=1 returns 2 and 20 rows, ?page=2 returns 0 and 17 rows, ?page=3 returns 0 and 0 rows, and all three are 200 rather than 404 or 422 -- page is never silently ignored; the key set of every row object is exactly {reference, movie_title, hall_name, seat_count, group, showtime_starts_at, showtime_ends_at, booked_at, seats, total_paise} and nothing else, so no status, cancelled_at, refund_paise, refund_state, cancellation_reason, cancel_url, tax_paise, discount_paise, booking_fee_paise or qr key can be present on any row of either array; reference matches ^FR-[23456789ACDEFHJKMNPQRTVWXY]{4}-[23456789ACDEFHJKMNPQRTVWXY]{4}$ and seat_count is an integer between 1 and 10; showtime_starts_at, showtime_ends_at and booked_at are ISO-8601 carrying the cinema row's UTC offset -- "2026-08-20T14:00:00+05:30" and never the same instant as "2026-08-20T08:30:00Z" -- serialised by the server from the cinema row and never by the client; seats is an array of labels ordered by row letter then seat number compared as an integer, so a booking of F2 and F10 returns ["F2","F10"] and a booking of F7, F8, F9 created in the order F9, F7, F8 still returns ["F7","F8","F9"]; total_paise is a JSON integer equal to the sum of the snapshotted booking_seat.price_paise, so three seats at 45000, 54000 and 54000 return 153000 and never 1530.0 and never the string "$1,530.00"; page=0, page=1001, page_size=0, page_size=51 and group=other each return 422 VALIDATION_FAILED; with no session the endpoint returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED "Sign in to see your bookings."; a caller with no bookings at all returns 200 with two empty arrays and both total_ counts 0
SourceRef: P-ACC-10 EP-ACC-07 FR-ADR-036 FR-ADR-039 FR-ADR-015 FR-ADR-048 FR-ADR-013 FR-ADR-018 SRC-001 §5.4.2 SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01

Title: Classify a booking upcoming or past against ends_at, and order each group totally
AcceptanceCriteria: With showtime.starts_at=2026-08-20T08:30:00Z and showtime.ends_at=2026-08-20T11:05:00Z and the clock injected: at 2026-08-20T09:30:00Z the booking's group is "upcoming" although the film is running, at exactly 2026-08-20T11:05:00Z it is "past", and at 2026-08-20T11:06:00Z it is "past" -- the rule is now < ends_at for upcoming and now >= ends_at for past, evaluated against the injected clock in UTC and never against the container clock or the client clock; upcoming is ordered by showtime.starts_at ascending then booking.created_at descending then booking.id ascending, and past by showtime.starts_at descending then the same two tie-breakers, proved by seeding five bookings of which three share one starts_at and asserting the exact returned id order, then paging the group at page_size=2 across three requests and asserting every id appears exactly once and none is missing; SELECT is_nullable FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name='showtime' AND column_name='ends_at' returns NO, and ends_at is stored rather than derived from starts_at plus a runtime; no test in this story sleeps or reads the wall clock, asserted by rg -n 'time\.time|time\.monotonic|time\.perf_counter|datetime\.now|datetime\.utcnow|sleep\(' over this story's test module returning 0 hits
SourceRef: P-ACC-11 EP-ACC-07 EP-ACC-08 FR-ADR-018 FR-ADR-043 SRC-001 §5.4.2 SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01

Title: Scope every /api/me/ route to the caller on the router, and limit the reference lookup
AcceptanceCriteria: Customer A owns reference refA and customer B owns refB. Signed in as A: GET /api/me/bookings returns a non-empty list containing refA (assertion 1, which proves the query works); GET /api/me/bookings/{refB} returns 404 NOT_FOUND "No booking with that reference is on your account." (assertion 2, which proves it is scoped); signed in as B, GET /api/me/bookings/{refB} returns 200 (assertion 3, which proves the scoping is by identity and not by the data being absent) -- all three are required and a suite carrying only assertion 2 fails this story; a reference that has never existed returns the same 404 with the same body and the same code as refB did for A, so the endpoint is not an oracle; a manager session and an admin session calling GET /api/me/bookings each receive their own bookings only; the two /api/me/ operations in the running app's OpenAPI document declare parameters exactly {group, page, page_size} for EP-ACC-07 and {reference} for EP-ACC-08, and no request body at all, so no user_id, owner_id, on_behalf_of or override parameter is accepted anywhere under /api/me/; the ownership predicate is in the same statement as the lookup, asserted with a SQLAlchemy before_cursor_execute listener installed for the test -- the harness must install it, and this criterion is what requires it -- recording every statement issued while serving GET /api/me/bookings/{refB}: exactly one recorded statement selects FROM booking, and its text contains both reference and user_id inside a single WHERE clause, so a fetch-by-reference followed by an in-handler comparison records either two booking statements or one with no user_id and fails; the authorisation dependency is declared once, on the router, and no handler re-checks the caller itself: it is present in the dependencies=[...] list of the router that mounts /api/me/, both the EP-ACC-07 and EP-ACC-08 route objects carry it in route.dependant.dependencies, and inspect.signature() of each of the two handler functions declares no parameter annotated with that dependency's return type; the reference is normalised case-insensitively with hyphens and whitespace ignored and the FR prefix optional, and a character outside the 26-character alphabet is not mapped to anything -- FR-0BCD-EFGH normalises to 0BCDEFGH, the 0 is not read as an O, and it produces the same 404 with the same body; the 21st lookup in a minute for one user returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After: 3 and "Too many lookups. Try again in 3 seconds.", the 61st lookup in a minute from one IP -- the 60 before it spread across four signed-in customers at 15 each, so no per-user bucket of 20 fills first -- returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After: 1 and "Too many lookups. Try again in 1 second." in the singular, and what is asserted is that the 61st call is refused, never which of the four customers issues it; GET /api/me/bookings itself is unlimited -- 100 consecutive calls all return 200 and none carries a Retry-After header

Title: Carry the seat selection through the registration detour without taking a hold
AcceptanceCriteria: An unauthenticated visitor on /showtimes/412 with seat ids 1187 and 1188 selected who leaves for the authentication screen by either route -- the primary action reading "Sign in to hold these seats" or the header's Sign in link -- has sessionStorage["fr.pending_selection"] equal to {"showtime_id":412,"seat_ids":[1187,1188],"stored_at":"2026-08-14T10:00:00Z"} written before /sign-in opens, and both routes render the context note "Your seats are still selected. Sign in to hold them."; fr.pending_selection and fr.selection are two distinct keys and both are present in sessionStorage at that moment, so a build in which one key serves both purposes fails this story; after a 201 from register or a 200 from sign-in the client navigates to /showtimes/412 and issues GET /api/showtimes/412/seatmap before restoring anything, then re-selects only the stored ids that response still reports available; stored ids now sold or held by another customer are not selected and carry their published accessible name from SCR-SEA-01 -- a now-sold C12 reads "Row C seat 12, Premium, sold" and a now-held C13 reads "Row C seat 13, Premium, held by someone else" -- and they are named in the message: "C12 and C13 were taken while you were signing in. Your other seats are still selected." at two or more, "C12 was taken while you were signing in. Your other seats are still selected." at exactly one, and "The seats you chose were taken while you were signing in. Choose again from the map." when none survives; the restore then removes fr.pending_selection from sessionStorage (sessionStorage.getItem("fr.pending_selection") is null) and leaves fr.selection holding the restored selection; no hold is taken by the restore -- the captured network log contains zero requests to POST /api/showtimes/412/holds between the sign-in response and the customer pressing the primary action, which now reads "Hold these seats"; a stored entry whose stored_at is more than 30 minutes before the browser's clock is discarded and the map opens with no selection and no message -- stored_at is written from that same browser clock, which the browser test harness installs before the page loads, and the server's injected clock does not reach this decision, so nothing here depends on the two agreeing; with sessionStorage unavailable (its getItem and setItem throwing) nothing is stored, no message is shown, the sign-in still succeeds and the map opens with no selection; a stored showtime_id that no longer exists returns the visitor to the movie listing with "That showtime is no longer available."; after sign-out, Object.keys(sessionStorage).filter(k => k.startsWith("fr.")).length is 0 -- the whole fr. namespace is swept, not a named list of keys
StatusNote: The feature is still unbuilt. No code writes fr.pending_selection: session.ts only reads and removes it. Nothing exists for the restore after sign-in, the "taken while you were signing in" messages or the no-hold check. The captured network log also needs a real browser.

Title: Measure the booking run against 120 seconds and report the first-time figure separately
AcceptanceCriteria: A scripted run marks t0 as the moment the seat map is first painted with real seat data -- the first moment at which the accessibility tree contains an element whose accessible name matches ^Row [A-Z]+ seat [0-9]+, .+, (available|sold|held by someone else|held by you|out of service)$, which is SCR-SEA-01's published form -- and not the click that requested the map and not the paint of the page shell; and t1 as the first moment the confirmation screen renders an element whose entire text content matches ^FR-[23456789ACDEFHJKMNPQRTVWXY]{4}-[23456789ACDEFHJKMNPQRTVWXY]{4}$ -- the pattern is anchored at both ends, so it is matched against that element's whole text and never against a substring of the screen; there are two measured sets and therefore two report lines, each named by a prefix that is part of its own anchored pattern, and the run's captured stdout is exactly these three lines and no fourth, so there is nowhere for a blended figure to appear: line 1 matches ^signed-in: [0-9]+ runs; slowest [0-9]+ s; median [0-9]+ s$, for example the literal line "signed-in: 20 runs; slowest 84 s; median 51 s"; line 2 matches ^first-time: [0-9]+ runs; slowest [0-9]+ s; median [0-9]+ s$, for example the literal line "first-time: 20 runs; slowest 96 s; median 63 s"; line 3 matches ^expired: [0-9]+ of [0-9]+ signed-in runs, [0-9]+ of [0-9]+ first-time runs ended 409 HOLD_EXPIRED$, for example the literal line "expired: 1 of 20 signed-in runs, 0 of 20 first-time runs ended 409 HOLD_EXPIRED" -- a line carrying the figures without its prefix fails its pattern, and so does a line reading "about 50 seconds"; the runs integer is 20 on line 1 and 20 on line 2, being the number of runs performed in each set and not the number that finished, while slowest and median on each line are computed over that set's runs which reached t1; the criterion passes when the integer captured for slowest on line 1 is less than 120, and the median figure decides nothing; a first-time run is one with no account at t0, including pressing "Sign in to hold these seats", registering and returning through fr.pending_selection, and line 2 carries no target -- the strings "PASS" and "FAIL" appear nowhere in the three lines and no line reports a figure computed from both sets; the measured path includes the simulated payment's PAYMENT_SIMULATED_DELAY_MS in full (the unit is milliseconds, so a configured 1500 is 1.5 s of the budget, not 1500 s), asserted by reading the value back from the running app's configuration and requiring it greater than 0, and by the captured network log for every run containing exactly one POST /api/showtimes/{showtime_id}/holds and exactly one POST /api/bookings, so no run can skip the simulated payment; a run in which the 180-second hold TTL expires mid-run receives 409 HOLD_EXPIRED with "The hold on your seats has ended and they have been released. You have not been charged." on its POST /api/bookings, reaches no t1, is one of the 20 the runs integer on its line counts, and is the run line 3 reports -- so an expired run is never dropped from the denominator and never silently absent
StatusNote: Needs a scripted real-browser run: 20 signed-in plus 20 first-time runs, measured from the accessibility tree with a network log, printing the three report lines. No such script or run exists. The 2026-11-07 Playwright flow is one booking, not this measurement.
SourceRef: P-ACC-15 FR-ADR-046 FR-ADR-041 FR-ADR-027 SRC-001 §3.1

Title: Enforce admin authorisation once, on the /api/admin router
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/admin/movies with no session returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED; with a customer session 403 FORBIDDEN; with a manager session 403 FORBIDDEN; with an admin session 200. A test iterates every route in app.routes whose path starts with /api/admin - the 32 routes EP-ADM-01 to EP-ADM-32 of api/contract.json, EP-ADM-30 to EP-ADM-32 being the admin-grant routes (SRC-008 ROLE-1 and its ADDENDUM, S-ADM-30) - and asserts the callable require_admin is present in that route object's resolved dependency list; the assertion reads the route object and never the handler body. Ripgrep over backend/app/api/admin/ for the pattern role ==|role !=|role in |require_role|has_permission|is_admin returns 0 hits, and a test that walks the AST of every .py file under backend/app/api/admin/ finds no string literal equal to admin, manager or customer, so no handler restates the rule. A test iterates every route mounted on the manager router and asserts route.methods is a subset of the set GET, HEAD. The role is read from the user row and never from the session claims: holding one valid unexpired admin session, a direct UPDATE setting that user row's role column to customer makes the very next request carrying that same session return 403 FORBIDDEN. The 403 body for a movie id that exists and for one that does not differ in no field except error.request_id: both carry code FORBIDDEN, the message This page is for administrators. Your account cannot change films, showtimes, prices or halls. and no details key, and the test parses both bodies, deletes error.request_id from each - the envelope carries one on every error and it is unique per request, so the raw bytes legitimately differ there and nowhere else - and asserts the two remaining structures are equal, so the refusal never reveals whether the film exists.
StatusNote: Every clause passes against the 32 admin routes (EP-ADM-01..32, SRC-008 ROLE-1, cell amended 2026-11-07), and GET /api/admin/movies is mounted.

Title: Write an audit row in the same transaction as every privileged write
AcceptanceCriteria: audit_log carries id, occurred_at, a non-null actor_user_id that is a foreign key resolving to a real user row, actor_role, action, entity_type, entity_id, jsonb before, jsonb after and request_id; SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE actor_user_id IS NULL returns 0 after the whole suite has run. POST /api/admin/screens writes exactly one row with action screen.created, before null, and actor_user_id equal to the calling admin's id. With the audit insert forced to raise inside the transaction by a test double, SELECT count(*) FROM screen is unchanged and the response is 500 INTERNAL_ERROR whose message is byte-for-byte The server could not complete this request. If you need help, quote a1b2c3d4. with a1b2c3d4 replaced by this request's own request_id. The action vocabulary is a closed Python enum AuditAction whose members are exactly the actions P-ADM-19 lists: constructing AuditAction from the string screen.exploded raises ValueError, and a handler asked to write that action fails at the boundary before BEGIN - asserted by a connection-level statement listener that records zero statements for that request, with SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log and SELECT count(*) FROM screen both unchanged. Executed as the application database role, UPDATE audit_log SET action = 'x' raises SQLSTATE 42501 insufficient_privilege and so does DELETE FROM audit_log; SELECT and INSERT succeed as the same role. A 220-seat batch through POST /api/admin/screens/{screen_id}/seats writes exactly 220 rows with action seat.created, one per seat primary key, in the same transaction as the 220 seat rows. One request that changes a movie title and its display_until writes exactly two rows - one movie.updated whose before and after each hold exactly the key title, one movie.display_window_changed whose before and after each hold exactly the keys display_from and display_until - and a request that submits two fields and changes one writes exactly one row. The user row has exactly seven fields - id, email, password_hash, role, password_version, created_at, last_signed_in_at - and the two credential fields are excluded from every audit row: SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE entity_type = 'user' AND (before ?| array['password_hash','password_version'] OR after ?| array['password_hash','password_version']) returns 0, and the JSON key set of before and of after on every entity_type = 'user' row is a subset of the set email, role, created_at, last_signed_in_at. SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE before::text LIKE '%JFIF%' OR after::text LIKE '%JFIF%' OR before ?| array['card_number','pan','cvv'] OR after ?| array['card_number','pan','cvv'] returns 0. Ripgrep over backend/app backend/migrations and frontend/src for the pattern showtime[.]price_changed returns 0 hits; a change to a base price writes showtime.base_price_changed.
StatusNote: The migrated_db fixture now checks SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE actor_user_id IS NULL = 0 at the teardown of every module's database (backend/tests/dbkit.py, 2026-11-07), so a full-suite run covers every database the suite used; actor_user_id is also NOT NULL with an FK. Open: no full-suite run with that check has been recorded yet, so 'after the whole suite has run' is unverified. Every other clause passes.

Title: Read and edit the venue, its name and its IANA time zone
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/admin/cinemas returns an array ordered name ASC, id ASC, each item carrying id, name, timezone, screen_count and version. PATCH /api/admin/cinemas/{cinema_id} with a matching version and a new name returns 200, increments version by exactly 1 and writes one cinema.updated audit row. One request changing both the name and the zone writes exactly two audit rows, cinema.updated and cinema.timezone_changed, in the same transaction. A timezone value that zoneinfo.ZoneInfo() raises ZoneInfoNotFoundError for - for example Asia/Atlantis - returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with nothing written and version unchanged; a name of 121 characters after trimming returns 422, and a second row whose lower(trim(name)) matches an existing one returns 422. Title: Resolve every local time from the cinema row, never from CINEMA_TIMEZONE
AcceptanceCriteria: Ripgrep over backend/app backend/migrations , frontend/src and scripts/ for the literal CINEMA_TIMEZONE returns hits in exactly two files, backend/app/core/config.py and scripts/seed.py, and 0 hits under backend/app/api, backend/app/domain, backend/app/models, backend/app/workers, backend/app/jobs and frontend/src. With the cinema row set to Asia/Kolkata and CINEMA_TIMEZONE set to UTC, a showtime stored as 2026-08-14T14:00:00Z renders as 2026-08-14 19:30 (14:00 plus the 05:30 Asia/Kolkata offset), the process emits exactly one log line at level WARNING at boot whose JSON payload carries cinema_id, the row zone Asia/Kolkata and the variable value UTC, and GET /health/ready returns 200. With the cinema row edited to Asia/Dubai, SELECT starts_at for that showtime still returns 2026-08-14T14:00:00Z - the test compares the stored value before and after and asserts equality, so not one instant is rewritten - and the same showtime renders as 2026-08-14 18:00 (14:00 plus the 04:00 Asia/Dubai offset). With SELECT count(*) FROM cinema at 0 the process starts and emits exactly one WARNING line saying the venue has not been seeded. A connection-level statement listener over the whole boot sequence records only SELECT statements against cinema and no UPDATE and no ALTER. SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name IN ('showtime','screen') AND column_name LIKE '%timezone%' returns 0, so a showtime reaches its zone only as showtime to screen to cinema.timezone.

(3) The "exactly two files" rg is asserted over backend/app only, without scripts/seed.py.

Title: Lay out a hall's seats while it has no showtimes
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/screens/{screen_id}/seats accepts 1 to 500 seat objects, each carrying row_label of 1 to 4 letters, seat_number of 1 or more, grid_row and grid_col of 1 or more and a seat_category_id that exists; a 220-seat batch returns 201 with 220 items and writes 220 seat.created audit rows in the same transaction. A batch of 500 entries returns 201 and one of 501 returns 422. Fixture: the hall already holds C12, C13 and C14 and the admin submits the five seats C11, C12, C13, C14, C15 in that order. The response is 422 VALIDATION_FAILED, details is {"duplicate_labels": ["C12", "C13", "C14"]} in the order submitted, and message is byte-for-byte Seats C12, C13 and C14 already exist in this hall. Every seat in a hall needs its own row and number. Afterwards SELECT count(*) FROM seat WHERE screen_id = :id is unchanged, so C11 and C15 were not created either. The same five-seat batch against a hall holding only C13 returns details {"duplicate_labels": ["C13"]} and the singular message Seat C13 already exists in this hall. Every seat in a hall needs its own row and number.; the boundary is exactly one offending seat versus two or more. Two seats submitted at one (grid_row, grid_col), or one colliding with a stored seat, return 422 with details carrying duplicate_coordinates; at one offending seat the message is Another seat is already drawn at that position in the map. Choose a different position. and at three it is Another seat is already drawn at 3 of those positions in the map. Choose different positions. - a count and never a label. An unknown seat_category_id returns 422 with That seat category is not on the list. Choose one of the listed categories.; seat_number 0 returns 422; grid_row 0 returns 422; a row_label of 5 letters or one containing a digit returns 422 with Enter a row label of 1 to 4 letters, for example A or AA. On a hall where SELECT count(*) FROM showtime WHERE screen_id = :id is 0: PATCH /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} changing row_label, seat_number or seat_category_id returns 200 and writes one seat.updated row, and DELETE /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} returns 204 and writes one seat.deleted row. GET /api/admin/screens/{screen_id}/seats returns the seats ordered grid_row ASC, grid_col ASC, id ASC together with has_showtimes and showtime_count. Every seat write takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the screen row before writing: a test opens a second transaction holding that same row lock, fires the seat insert on another connection, and asserts that insert is waiting on it rather than proceeding - SELECT count(*) FROM pg_locks WHERE granted = false AND pid = the inserting backend's pid returns 1 while the insert has not returned - then releases the lock and asserts the insert completes. No clock, injected or real, is advanced to prove the wait, because a PostgreSQL row lock is held by the database and does not honour an application clock.
SourceRef: P-ADM-13 E6 S4 FR-ADR-016 FR-ADR-022 SRC-001 §9.3

Title: Freeze a hall's seat identity the moment any showtime exists on it
AcceptanceCriteria: With SELECT count(*) FROM showtime WHERE screen_id = :id greater than 0: PATCH /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} changing row_label returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN with the message Seat C12 cannot be renumbered. This hall has showtimes, and a seat number is what a past customer's ticket says. You can add a seat, or take a seat out of service. and SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log is unchanged across the request; changing seat_number gives the same 409 and the same sentence; changing seat_category_id returns 409 with Seat C12 cannot be moved to a different category. This hall has showtimes, and its seats are already priced. You can add a seat, or take a seat out of service.; DELETE /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} returns 409 with Seat C12 cannot be removed. This hall has showtimes, and removing a seat would break the record of who booked it. Take it out of service instead. The 409 details carry exactly the keys screen_id, seat_id, showtime_count and frozen_fields, and frozen_fields is the array ["row_label", "seat_number", "seat_category_id"]. In the same state, changing grid_row or grid_col returns 200, setting is_active returns 200, POST /api/admin/screens/{screen_id}/seats returns 201, and PATCH /api/admin/screens/{screen_id} renaming the hall returns 200. The state is decided by the count of showtime rows on the screen evaluated inside the transaction and not by whether they are future or booked: a hall carrying exactly one showtime whose starts_at is in the past and for which SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat is 0 refuses identically to a hall carrying one future sold-out showtime. Calling the domain function directly with a database session and no HTTP request raises LayoutFrozen carrying the same screen_id, seat_id and showtime_count, and ripgrep over backend/app/api/admin/ for the pattern showtime_count|LAYOUT_FROZEN returns 0 hits, so the check is not in the handler. A walk of app.routes finds exactly one mounted route whose request schema accepts a row_label field - PATCH /api/admin/seats/{seat_id}, EP-ADM-20 - and in this state it returns 409, so the only remedies are to take the mistyped seat out of service and add a correctly labelled one, or to wipe and reseed.
SourceRef: P-ADM-14 E6 S4 FR-ADR-022 FR-ADR-024 SRC-001 §9.3

Title: Materialise a showtime's seat set at creation and never move it
AcceptanceCriteria: On a screen with 90 seats where is_active is true, creating showtime 501 writes 90 showtime_seat rows and sets seat_count_at_creation to 90. Adding seat J11 then creating showtime 502 writes 91 rows and 91; setting J11 is_active false then creating showtime 503 writes 90 rows and 90; setting J11 is_active true again leaves SELECT count(*) FROM showtime_seat WHERE showtime_id = 503 at exactly 90, the same value the test recorded before the restoration, and creating showtime 504 afterwards writes 91. SELECT count(*) FROM showtime_seat WHERE showtime_id = 501 returns 90 at every point in this sequence, and a PATCH on any of the four showtimes leaves both seat_count_at_creation and the row count unchanged. SELECT count(*) FROM showtime s WHERE s.seat_count_at_creation <> (SELECT count(*) FROM showtime_seat ss WHERE ss.showtime_id = s.id) returns 0. Creating a showtime on a screen where the count of seats with is_active true is 0 returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN and SELECT count(*) FROM showtime is unchanged, so no showtime can carry a zero denominator. (showtime_id, seat_id) is unique on showtime_seat, and that index is not the oversell guard - the oversell guard stays the unique constraint on booking_seat (showtime_id, seat_id), and a test asserts both indexes exist by name in information_schema. A walk of app.routes finds no mounted route whose path contains showtime_seat and none matching /api/admin/showtimes/{showtime_id}/seats; POST /api/admin/showtimes/501/seats and DELETE /api/admin/showtimes/501/seats/77 each return 404 NOT_FOUND with the message That page does not exist. With the seat-set INSERT forced to raise by a test double, SELECT count(*) FROM showtime is unchanged and the response is 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE with the message The system cannot reach its database right now. Nothing was saved. Try again in a moment.
SourceRef: P-ADM-14 E6 S4 FR-ADR-022 FR-ADR-024 SRC-002 §8.1.5

Title: Create a showtime by hand, and let nothing else create one
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/showtimes with movie_id, screen_id, naive local starts_at and ends_at, base_price_paise and an optional format_id returns 201 with version 1 and writes one showtime.created audit row. starts_at 2026-09-04 18:30 and ends_at 2026-09-04 20:58 for a 148-minute film store 2026-09-04T13:00:00Z and 2026-09-04T15:28:00Z, each the local value less the 05:30 Asia/Kolkata offset, and the 201 body returns both as the strings 2026-09-04T18:30:00 and 2026-09-04T20:58:00 with no Z and no offset. A starts_at or ends_at carrying a trailing Z, a +hh:mm offset or a zone name returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED, and the test asserts the stored table is unchanged, so the value is never coerced. The film need not be published: a showtime created against a movie whose published_at is null returns 201. A screen whose is_active is false returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN with This hall is out of service. Bring it back into service before creating showtimes on it.; a screen with zero seats in service returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN; an unknown movie_id or screen_id returns 404; ends_at equal to starts_at returns 422 and ends_at one minute before starts_at returns 422. A format_id naming a row whose is_active is false returns 422, while a showtime already carrying that format_id still returns it on a GET. If the film carries a display window, a starts_at outside display_from <= starts_at < display_until returns 422 and SELECT count(*) FROM showtime, FROM showtime_seat and FROM audit_log are each unchanged; a film whose display_from and display_until are both null accepts any starts_at, which is the draft case. A starts_at in the past relative to the injected clock returns 201, because the seed needs about a month of history. The insert runs inside SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the screen row, asserted the same way as in S-ADM-06. Ripgrep over backend/app backend/migrations and scripts/ for the pattern (?i)INSERT INTO showtime\b|insert\(showtime\) returns hits in exactly two files, backend/app/domain/admin/showtimes.py and scripts/seed.py, and 0 hits under backend/app/workers and backend/app/jobs; ripgrep over backend/app backend/migrations , frontend/src , scripts/ and .github/workflows/ for the pattern APScheduler|celery|crontab|cron.d|schedule[.]every|EventBridge returns 0 hits - the code trees are named explicitly rather than scanning the repository root, because this criterion's own text carries every one of those literals once the backlog lives in docs/05 Bible/ and a root scan could never pass. ends_at is stored and never derived from runtime_minutes: a PATCH changing that film's runtime_minutes from 148 to 120 leaves SELECT ends_at for every showtime of that film byte-identical to the value read before the PATCH.

Title: Refuse two overlapping showtimes on one hall
AcceptanceCriteria: Fixture: showtime 41 on Screen 3 stored as 2026-09-04 18:30 to 20:58 local, and no other showtime on Screen 3. A create at 20:45 to 22:40 returns 409 SHOWTIME_OVERLAP, because 18:30 < 22:40 and 20:58 > 20:45 are both true. A create at 20:58 to 22:53 returns 201, because 20:58 > 20:58 is false and the intervals are half-open, so an end instant equal to the next start is not an overlap. A create at 21:15 to 23:10 returns 201. The 409 details carry conflicts, and conflicts is a JSON array in every case - never an object and never null - whose entries each hold exactly showtime_id, movie_title, starts_at and ends_at with the two instants in naive local form; against one conflicting stored showtime len(conflicts) is 1 and against two it is 2. The predicate is starts_at < :new_ends_at AND ends_at > :new_starts_at, run inside the same SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the screen row as the insert, and on an edit it carries AND id <> :this_id, asserted by a query-log capture of the statement the request issues. Two overlapping creates fired concurrently against one screen produce exactly one 201 and exactly one 409, and SELECT count(*) FROM showtime WHERE screen_id = :id increases by exactly 1. No changeover minimum is enforced anywhere: the zero-gap create above returns 201, and ripgrep over backend/app backend/migrations , frontend/src and scripts/ for the pattern turnaround|changeover|MIN_GAP|MINIMUM_GAP|cleanup_minutes returns 0 hits.

Title: Edit a showtime, and list one hall's day
AcceptanceCriteria: PATCH /api/admin/showtimes/{showtime_id} changing base_price_paise writes exactly one showtime.base_price_changed audit row; changing starts_at writes exactly one showtime.updated; one request changing both writes exactly two rows. A body carrying a screen_id different from the stored one returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log is unchanged. seat_count_at_creation and SELECT count(*) FROM showtime_seat WHERE showtime_id = :id are unchanged by every edit in this story. Bounds are evaluated against the merged row: with 18:30 to 20:58 stored, a PATCH carrying only starts_at 20:58 returns 422, a PATCH carrying only starts_at 21:30 returns 422, and a PATCH carrying only ends_at 18:30 returns 422; the overlap predicate of S-ADM-10 also runs against the merged interval with AND id <> :this_id. Editing a showtime that already has bookings changes nothing about them: SELECT price_paise FROM booking_seat WHERE booking_id = :b is identical before and after, and a customer holding seats at the moment the start is moved 60 minutes earlier still holds them, asserted by the hold token still resolving in Redis after the 200. Fixture for the list, four showtimes on Screen 3 and no others: 601 starts 2026-09-04 10:00 local = 04:30:00Z, 602 starts 14:00 local = 08:30:00Z, 603 starts 18:35 local = 13:05:00Z, 604 starts 21:30 local = 16:00:00Z. GET /api/admin/showtimes?screen_id=3&date=2026-09-04 at the injected request instant 2026-09-04T13:05:00Z returns 601, 602, 603, 604 ordered by starts_at when include_past is absent or true, and returns only 604 when include_past is false: 603 is omitted because the boundary is starts_at <= now and its starts_at is exactly now. The endpoint accepts no page and no limit parameter - a walk of the route's query-parameter schema finds exactly screen_id, date and include_past - and returns the day whole. A missing or non-integer screen_id returns 422, an unknown screen_id 404, a date of 2026-13-45 returns 422 and include_past=maybe returns 422. now is taken once per request from the injected clock: the test freezes the clock, and ripgrep over backend/app for the pattern datetime[.]now[(][)]|datetime[.]utcnow|time[.]time[(][)] returns 0 hits outside backend/app/core/clock.py.

Title: Set a base price per showtime in integer paise
AcceptanceCriteria: base_price_paise is stored as a bigint and accepted only as an integer number of paise: a body carrying 25000.5 returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with the message Enter the base price in whole cents. A price cannot have a fraction of a cent. and the test asserts nothing was stored, so it is never rounded. A missing value returns 422 with Enter a base price for this showtime.; 0 returns 422 and -1 returns 422, each with The base price must be at least 1 cent.; 1 returns 201. The arithmetic ceiling is base_price_paise * (10000 + highest stored uplift_basis_points) + 5000 <= 9223372036854775807, which is 2^63 - 1. With the highest stored uplift_basis_points at 3333, so the multiplier is 13333: 691770197019033 * 13333 + 5000 = 9223372036854771989, which is at most 9223372036854775807, so that base price returns 201; 691770197019034 * 13333 + 5000 = 9223372036854785322, which is above it, so that base price returns 422 with That base price is too large for this system to hold. Enter a smaller amount. The bound is written against the highest stored uplift and not against a constant, so with a fourth category added at 6666 basis points the multiplier becomes 16666 and 691770197019033 then returns 422. Reading docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json, the endpoint objects with id EP-ADM-10 and EP-ADM-11 each contain the literal substring base_price_paise * (10000 + highest stored uplift_basis_points) + 5000 must be <= 2^63 - 1, so the bound is in the generated artefact and not in prose alone. The interface converts dollars to cents at its boundary: entering 250.00 in the dollar field produces a request body carrying base_price_paise 25000 as an integer, asserted by capturing the body the form submits. The minor-unit ratio and the currency code each exist as one named configuration value, CURRENCY_MINOR_UNIT_RATIO (default 100) and CURRENCY_CODE (USD), the S7.9 names, both declared in backend/app/core/config.py. Ripgrep over backend/app for the pattern [*/]\s*100\b, excluding backend/app/core/config.py and backend/app/domain/money.py, returns 0 hits. No business upper bound is enforced: a base_price_paise of 2500000 returns 201, and GET on that showtime's seat map returns price_paise 2812500 for a seat at 1250 basis points, from 2500000 * 11250 + 5000 = 28125005000, // 10000 = 2812500, so the mistyped figure prices through the S-ADM-13 formula unaltered and nothing clamps it.
StatusNote: Now asserted (tests/adm/test_s_adm_12.py, 2026-11-07): the seat-map GET returns price_paise 2812500 for a 1250-basis-point seat on a showtime POSTed at 2500000; CURRENCY_MINOR_UNIT_RATIO (100) and CURRENCY_CODE (USD) declared in core/config.py; the [*/]\s*100 sweep excludes exactly core/config.py and domain/money.py. One clause open: 'capturing the body the form submits' for 250.00 in the dollar field needs a DOM submit event and the frontend has no DOM test environment (money.test.mjs tests the conversion function).
SourceRef: P-ADM-10 E6 S4 FR-ADR-036 FR-ADR-037 FR-ADR-038 SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-01 SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01

Title: Apply one percentage uplift per seat category, uniformly, with integer half-up rounding
AcceptanceCriteria: The seat price is seat_price_paise = (base_price_paise * (10000 + uplift_basis_points) + BASIS_POINT_HALF) // BASIS_POINT_SCALE with BASIS_POINT_SCALE = 10000 and BASIS_POINT_HALF = 5000 as named constants, integer throughout: ripgrep over backend/app/domain/pricing.py for the pattern float[(]|Decimal[(]|[.]5|round[(] returns 0 hits, and for the bare literals 10000 or 5000 returns hits only on the two constant definitions. At base_price_paise 25000 the three categories at 0, 1250 and 3333 basis points produce exactly 25000, 28125 and 33333 paise, and each is shown: 25000 * 10000 + 5000 = 250005000, // 10000 = 25000; 25000 * 11250 + 5000 = 281255000, // 10000 = 28125; 25000 * 13333 + 5000 = 333330000, // 10000 = 33333. The 3333 line is the deciding case and the test asserts it explicitly: the exact value is 33332.5 paise, integer half-up gives 33333 and half-even would give 33332, and the assertion is 33333. The carry is exercised in the other direction too: at base_price_paise 24999 with 3333 basis points, 24999 * 13333 + 5000 = 333316667, // 10000 = 33331, because the exact value 33331.1667 is below a half. Rounding is per seat and the total is never rounded: three seats at 3333 basis points on a base of 25000 total 3 * 33333 = 99999 paise exactly and never 99998, and the test asserts 99999. POST /api/admin/seat-categories and PATCH /api/admin/seat-categories/{seat_category_id} accept an integer uplift_basis_points of 0 or more; -1 returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with The uplift cannot be negative. This system has no discounts. and 1250.5 returns 422 with Enter the uplift in whole basis points. 100 basis points is 1 percent. The mirror arithmetic ceiling is the same inequality solved for the uplift instead of the base price: (highest stored base_price_paise) * (10000 + uplift_basis_points) + 5000 <= 9223372036854775807. Fixture: exactly one showtime is stored and its base_price_paise is 25000, so uplift_basis_points 368934881464190 is accepted because 25000 * (10000 + 368934881464190) + 5000 = 9223372036854755000, which is at most 9223372036854775807, and 368934881464191 returns 422 because it gives 9223372036854780000, which is above it, with the message That uplift is too large for this system to hold. Enter a smaller value. It is written against the highest stored base price and not against a constant, so raising that showtime's base_price_paise to 50000 makes 368934881464190 return 422 in turn. A name colliding on lower(trim(name)) returns 422 with A seat category with that name already exists.; a fourth category with an unused name returns 201; a walk of app.routes finds no route mounted for DELETE on /api/admin/seat-categories/{seat_category_id} and the request returns 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED. GET /api/admin/seat-categories returns affected_future_showtimes and evaluated_at_utc, where the count is COUNT(showtime WHERE starts_at + SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES > evaluated_at) across every hall, film and category, counting halls whose is_active is false and counting showtimes whose starts_at is already past. Fixture: four showtimes and no others in the database - A starts 2026-08-14 13:00 local = 2026-08-14T07:30:00Z, B starts 14:20 local = 08:50:00Z, C starts 14:30 local = 09:00:00Z, D starts 2026-08-16 19:30 local = 2026-08-16T14:00:00Z. At the injected instant 2026-08-14T09:00:00Z with SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES at +15 the four thresholds are 07:45:00Z, 09:05:00Z, 09:15:00Z and 2026-08-16T14:15:00Z; A fails because 07:45 > 09:00 is false, B, C and D each pass, so the response carries exactly 3. With the same four rows at the same instant and SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES reversed to -15 the thresholds become 07:15:00Z, 08:35:00Z, 08:45:00Z and 2026-08-16T13:45:00Z; only D passes, so the response carries exactly 1. The two evaluations are never compared: advancing the injected clock from 09:00:00Z to 09:10:00Z between the read and the write makes the GET return 3 and the PATCH response return 2 - B's threshold 09:05 is now past - and the PATCH still returns 200 with no warning key and no second confirmation in either body. One request changing a category's name and its uplift writes exactly two audit rows, seat_category.updated and seat_category.uplift_changed. Standard is a row whose uplift_basis_points is 0 and runs through the same formula: ripgrep over backend/app/domain/pricing.py for the pattern uplift_basis_points == 0|if not uplift|Standard returns 0 hits.
SourceRef: P-ADM-11 E6 S4 FR-ADR-038 FR-ADR-037 FR-ADR-016 SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-01 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-01

Title: Refuse a stale admin write, and make a write that changes nothing write nothing
AcceptanceCriteria: SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND column_name = 'version' returns exactly movie, showtime, screen, seat_category and cinema; seat is absent, and the request schema of PATCH /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} carries no version field, asserted by walking that route's body model fields. Every admin GET that feeds a form returns version in its body. A write with no version key returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and the stored row is unchanged, so it is never treated as last-write-wins. A stale version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT with the stored row unchanged and SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log unchanged; a successful write increments version by exactly 1. The ordering version, validation, no-op, write is asserted in three cases: a request carrying version 3 when the row holds 4 and submitting field values identical to the stored ones returns 409 and not 200; a request carrying the current version and a name of 61 characters returns 422 and not a 200 no-op, even when that 61-character value is the value already stored; and a request carrying the current version in which every submitted field already equals the stored value returns 200 with the row and its unchanged version, leaves the row byte-identical, does not increment version and leaves SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log unchanged. A request submitting two fields of which one differs writes the change, increments version by exactly 1 and writes exactly one audit row, whose action names the field that actually changed. On a seat, setting is_active to the value it already holds returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN while resubmitting an unchanged grid_row returns 200 with SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log unchanged, so the exemption is scoped to is_active alone. On POST /api/admin/movies/{movie_id}/poster the version arrives as a second form part of the multipart body and not as a header and not as a query parameter - a request putting it in either returns 422 - and the check order is Content-Length, then version, then declared content type and magic bytes, then decode and dimensions, then the S3 PutObject, so a stale version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT and a ListObjectsV2 on the posters/{movie_id}/ prefix afterwards returns the same key count as before the request. Each of the five admin edit forms - SCR-ADM-02 film editor, SCR-ADM-03 showtimes, SCR-ADM-04 seat categories, SCR-ADM-05 hall configuration and SCR-ADM-08 venue - is submitted unchanged by a test that captures the outgoing request body and asserts it carries an integer version equal to the value the preceding GET returned.
StatusNote: The poster multipart version clause is now proved in tests/adm/test_s_adm_25.py (version only as a form part, stale 409, no object written). Still open: the five admin edit forms submitted unchanged, with the captured request body carrying the GET's version. That needs a DOM or browser submit.

Title: Charge the price that was current when the hold was granted
AcceptanceCriteria: At T0 a hold on C12 (Premium, 1250 basis points) and C13 (Standard, 0) on a showtime with base_price_paise 25000 writes per-seat prices 28125 and 25000 into the Redis hold value under the hold token, alongside the two seat ids and an absolute expiry instant; the test reads the Redis key back and asserts those five fields. Those two figures follow from the S-ADM-13 formula: 25000 * 11250 + 5000 = 281255000, // 10000 = 28125, and 25000 * 10000 + 5000 = 250005000, // 10000 = 25000. At T0+40s an admin sets base_price_paise to 30000; the write returns 200, increments version by exactly 1 and writes one showtime.base_price_changed audit row with before {"base_price_paise": 25000} and after {"base_price_paise": 30000} - it is never refused because a hold exists. At T0+95s the confirm reads the held prices and writes booking_seat rows with price_paise 28125 and 25000, base_price_paise_applied 25000 on both, uplift_basis_points_applied 1250 and 0, and booking.total_paise 28125 + 25000 = 53125; nothing is recomputed from the showtime row, asserted by the two price_paise values not being 33750 and 30000. A hold taken at T0+120s on a Premium seat and a Standard seat of the same showtime other than C12 and C13 - which the T0+95s confirm sold, and a seat is never sold twice (SRC-001 §2.2) - is quoted 33750 and 30000, from 30000 * 11250 + 5000 = 337505000, // 10000 = 33750 and 30000 * 10000 + 5000 = 300005000, // 10000 = 30000. With SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS at 180 the hold key carries that expiry and expires on its own: against real Redis, PTTL on the hold key immediately after acquisition returns a value in the range 179000 to 180000 inclusive, and expiry itself is asserted against the Redis test double the harness supplies, whose key expiry is driven by the same injected clock as every other instant in this scenario, so EXISTS on the hold key returns true at T0+179s and false at T0+181s - the assertion names the double because real Redis honours its own wall-clock TTL and knows nothing of the injected clock, and against real Redis the key would still be present at both points. No cleanup job runs: ripgrep over backend/app for the pattern DEL hold|expire_holds|sweep_holds returns 0 hits. Every instant in this scenario comes from the injected clock and ripgrep over the test module for datetime[.]now[(][)]|time[.]time[(][)] returns 0 hits. The confirm transaction takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the showtime row, so an admin PATCH of that same row issued while the confirm is open waits on that lock rather than being refused: a test holds the confirm open, fires the PATCH, asserts the PATCH has not returned and that SELECT count(*) FROM pg_locks WHERE granted = false AND pid = the PATCH's backend pid returns 1, then commits the confirm and asserts the PATCH returns 200 - not 409 and not any hold-related refusal - and that SELECT price_paise FROM booking_seat WHERE booking_id = the committed booking still returns 28125 and 25000.
StatusNote: EP-PAY-01 now exists, but these clauses have no test: the T0+95s confirm writing booking_seat 28125/25000 with total 53125; the admin PATCH waiting on the confirm's showtime row lock (pg_locks), then 200; and EXISTS at T0+179s/181s against an injected-clock Redis double, which the harness does not supply.

Title: Take a seat out of service and return it
AcceptanceCriteria: PATCH /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} with is_active false returns 200 and writes one seat.deactivated audit row with before {"is_active": true} and after {"is_active": false}; with is_active true it writes seat.reactivated. Setting is_active to the value the seat already holds returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN with the message Seat C12 is already out of service. in the false case and Seat C12 is already in service. in the true case, not a 200 no-op. The write takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the seat's screen row, asserted the same way as in S-ADM-06, so it cannot land half inside a concurrent showtime creation. A retired seat is absent from the showtime_seat set of every showtime created after the change and present on the set of every showtime created before it: SELECT count(*) FROM showtime_seat WHERE showtime_id = :existing and SELECT seat_count_at_creation FROM showtime WHERE id = :existing are each identical before and after the toggle, and SELECT count(*) FROM showtime_seat WHERE showtime_id = :created_after AND seat_id = :id returns 0. A seat already sold on an existing showtime stays sold: SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE seat_id = :id is identical before and after the toggle, and GET /api/me/bookings/{reference} for that booking still renders the seat's original row_label and seat_number. Returning a seat to service does not add it to any showtime created while it was out of service: the count for :created_while_out is unchanged by the reactivation. A walk of app.routes finds no mounted path containing the segment cancel and none containing the segment refund anywhere in the application.
StatusNote: GET /api/me/bookings/{reference} now exists, but no test asserts that it still renders the retired seat's original row_label and seat_number.
SourceRef: P-ADM-15 E6 S4 FR-ADR-022 FR-ADR-012

Title: Withdraw a hall without cancelling anything
AcceptanceCriteria: PATCH /api/admin/screens/{screen_id} with is_active false and a matching version returns 200, increments version by exactly 1 and writes one screen.deactivated audit row; is_active true writes screen.reactivated. POST /api/admin/showtimes naming a screen whose is_active is false returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN with the message This hall is out of service. Bring it back into service before creating showtimes on it. SELECT count(*) FROM showtime WHERE screen_id = :id, SELECT count(*) FROM seat WHERE screen_id = :id and SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat joined to that screen are each identical before and after the withdrawal, and GET /api/me/bookings/{reference} for a booking on that hall still renders the hall's name. GET /api/reports for that hall still returns a row for it after the withdrawal, because the record points at screen_id and not at a name string. A stale version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT with the row unchanged and SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log unchanged. A walk of app.routes finds no route mounted for DELETE on /api/admin/screens/{screen_id}; the request returns 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED with the message That action is not available. Nothing was changed., and SELECT count(*) FROM screen is unchanged by every request in this story. SCR-ADM-05 renders the withdrawal confirmation with the byte-for-byte text This hall will accept no new showtimes. Showtimes that already exist are not changed, bookings are not cancelled, and nothing is refunded. The hall is not deleted and you can bring it back into service.

Still not tested: GET /api/me/bookings/{reference} rendering the hall name after withdrawal, and GET /api/reports returning a row for the withdrawn hall. Both endpoints exist. The SCR-ADM-05 confirmation is checked in source by rg, not rendered.
