Title: Create a manager account and assign it halls
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/managers with an email and screen_ids creates, in one transaction, a user row with role manager, one manager_screen_assignment row per screen, one manager.created audit row and one manager.screen_assigned row per assignment, and returns 201 with the id, email and assigned screen ids. No usable password means this, and each part is asserted: the new row's password_hash is NOT NULL and is a bcrypt digest, password_version is 1, last_signed_in_at is null, two managers created in the same test have different password_hash values so no shared sentinel is written, and POST /api/auth/login with that email and any password returns 401 CREDENTIALS_INVALID with the message That email address and password do not match an account. A body carrying a role property returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID and SELECT count(*) FROM the user table is unchanged. No endpoint creates an admin account: a test replays every mounted POST and PUT route under /api/admin with a body carrying role admin and asserts SELECT count(*) FROM the user table WHERE role = 'admin' is unchanged by all of them, and ripgrep over backend/app backend/migrations for the pattern role\s*=\s*.admin. returns hits only in scripts/seed.py. An email already used by any account returns 422 with An account already exists with that email address. Accounts are never removed, so an address stays in use once it has been registered.; a malformed address returns 422; a screen_id that does not exist returns 422; the same screen_id twice in the array returns 422 with That hall is listed twice. Choose each hall once. An empty screen_ids array returns 201 and GET on that manager's dashboard returns 200 with an empty rows array rather than an error. PUT /api/admin/managers/{user_id}/screens replaces the complete set, writing one manager.screen_assigned row per addition and one manager.screen_unassigned row per removal; the unassignment row's entity_type is manager_screen_assignment, its entity_id is the primary key the removed row held, its before carries exactly the keys user_id and screen_id and its after is null, and afterwards SELECT count(*) FROM manager_screen_assignment WHERE id = :that_entity_id returns 0 while SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.referential_constraints joined to information_schema.key_column_usage on constraint_name and constraint_schema (referential_constraints carries constraint names and rules but no table and no column, so it cannot on its own decide which foreign key exists) for a foreign key on audit_log.entity_id returns 0. A target user_id that exists but whose role is not manager returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with That account is not a manager account. Screens can only be assigned to managers. (user_id, screen_id) is unique on manager_screen_assignment, asserted by name in information_schema. Nothing enforces two managers per hall, asserted as artefacts and not as an intention: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'manager_screen_assignment'::regclass AND contype = 'c' returns 0, SELECT count(*) FROM pg_trigger WHERE tgrelid = 'manager_screen_assignment'::regclass AND NOT tgisinternal returns 0, and the behaviour is proved positively - assigning a third manager to one hall returns 201, and a hall with zero managers assigned returns 200 with an empty rows array from the dashboard. GET /api/admin/managers returns the accounts ordered email ASC, user_id ASC with has_signed_in equal to (last_signed_in_at IS NOT NULL) and no has_signed_in column present in information_schema.columns. The create writes no outbox_message row and enqueues no SES message: SELECT count(*) FROM outbox_message is unchanged across the request and the SES test double records zero calls. The user row has exactly seven fields and the two credential fields are excluded from every audit row: SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE before ?| array['password_hash','password_version'] OR after ?| array['password_hash','password_version'] returns 0, and the JSON key set of before and after on every entity_type = 'user' row is a subset of the set email, role, created_at, last_signed_in_at.
StatusNote: Login refusal for the new manager is now asserted. Still open: "An empty screen_ids array ... GET on that manager's dashboard returns 200 with an empty rows array" (the dashboard exists, but there is no test).

Title: Withdraw instead of deleting, everywhere
AcceptanceCriteria: A test enumerating every mounted route finds exactly two whose method is DELETE and whose path starts with /api/admin - DELETE /api/admin/seats/{seat_id}, EP-ADM-21, and DELETE /api/admin/admin-grants/{grant_id}, EP-ADM-32 (SRC-008 ROLE-1 and its ADDENDUM, S-ADM-30) - and no DELETE route for movie, showtime, screen, cinema or any lookup vocabulary. DELETE against /api/admin/movies/{movie_id}, /api/admin/showtimes/{showtime_id}, /api/admin/screens/{screen_id}, /api/admin/cinemas/{cinema_id}, /api/admin/lookups/{kind} and /api/admin/lookups/{kind}/{id} each return 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED whose body is the product's single error envelope with the message That action is not available. Title: Upload a poster to private object storage
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/movies/{movie_id}/poster is multipart/form-data carrying exactly one file part and one version form part, and the checks run in the order Content-Length, version, declared content type and magic bytes, decode and pixel dimensions, then S3 PutObject, then the movie row and its audit row in one transaction; the order is asserted by a request that fails two checks at once always returning the earlier one's status. Content-Length absent returns 422; Content-Length 2097152 returns 201 and 2097153 returns 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE with the request body never read, asserted by the test server recording 0 bytes consumed from the request stream. A declared content type outside image/jpeg, image/png and image/webp returns 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE; a part declared image/png whose leading bytes are the JPEG magic FF D8 FF returns 415; a part declared image/png whose bytes are not a decodable image returns 415. Pixel dimensions 200 by 300 return 201 and 199 by 300 return 422; 4000 by 6000 return 201 and 4001 by 6000 return 422. Zero file parts returns 422 and two file parts returns 422. A missing version form part returns 422; version sent as a header or as a query parameter instead returns 422. A stale version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT and a ListObjectsV2 on posters/{movie_id}/ afterwards returns the same key count as before the request. A success stores the object at a key matching ^posters/\d+/[0-9a-f]{32}$ that contains no part of the client's filename - a file uploaded as my poster.png produces a key in which the substring poster appears only as the fixed prefix and my does not appear at all - sets poster_object_key inside the transaction after re-reading and re-comparing version, increments version by exactly 1, and writes one movie.poster_uploaded audit row on the first upload and movie.poster_replaced on every later one with the previous key in before. After a replacement, a GetObject on the previous key still returns 200 with the original bytes. GET /api/admin/movies/{movie_id}/poster returns 302 whose Location carries X-Amz-Expires=3600; GetPublicAccessBlock on the bucket reports BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy and RestrictPublicBuckets all true and GetBucketPolicy returns no statement granting s3:GetObject to Principal *; an unauthenticated GET of the object URL returns 403. A draft film's poster is reachable through this admin endpoint and GET /api/movies/{movie_id}/poster for that film returns 404. An S3 5xx or a throttling error returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE, and a non-retryable refusal returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with the message The server could not complete this request. If you need help, quote {request_id}. carrying this request's id. A test snapshots the listings of the process working directory and of tempfile.gettempdir() before and after the request and asserts both are unchanged, so nothing is written to the container's local disk. A walk of app.routes finds no mounted path matching the case-insensitive regex bucket|storage|usage|quota and no DELETE route whose path contains poster, and GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration on the bucket returns no rules, so nothing in the product reports the finite 5 GB allowance and nothing removes an object to stay inside it. REQUEST ID: every {request_id} above is read from this response's error.request_id (or the X-Request-Id header) at assertion time and matches ^[0-9a-f]{8}$; it is never compared to a literal, because the envelope generates a fresh id on every error and an inbound X-Request-Id is never trusted.
StatusNote: These wait for AWS (on hold by the client): GetPublicAccessBlock, GetBucketPolicy, an unauthenticated GET answering 403, GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration, and ListObjectsV2/GetObject against the real bucket (Zone C). There is also a conflict. The cell says GET /api/movies/{id}/poster returns 404 for a draft film, but the now-mounted route applies no visibility gate, and the test asserts 302 (S-BRW-18's reading). That needs a ruling or an amendment.

Title: Set a film's display window in naive local time
AcceptanceCriteria: display_from and display_until are accepted as naive local Asia/Kolkata values; a value carrying a trailing Z, a +hh:mm offset or a zone name returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and the stored columns are unchanged, so it is never coerced. Entering display_from 2026-09-04 00:00 and display_until 2026-10-02 00:00 stores 2026-09-03T18:30:00Z and 2026-10-01T18:30:00Z, each the local value less the 05:30 Asia/Kolkata offset, and GET returns both as 2026-09-04T00:00:00 and 2026-10-02T00:00:00 with no Z and no offset. With the injected clock at 2026-10-01T18:29:59Z, GET /api/movies contains the film; with the clock at 2026-10-01T18:30:00Z it does not - so the last visible local day is 1 Oct 2026, because display_until is exclusive. The server adds no day, rounds nothing to midnight and derives neither end from the other: entering display_from 2026-09-04 09:15 stores 2026-09-04T03:45:00Z exactly, and submitting display_from alone leaves display_until unchanged. display_until equal to display_from returns 422 and display_until one minute before display_from returns 422, each with the row unchanged, SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log unchanged and version unchanged. The bound is evaluated against the merged row: with display_from 2026-09-01 00:00 and display_until 2026-09-30 00:00 stored, a PATCH carrying only display_from 2026-10-15 00:00 returns 422 and version is unchanged, and a PATCH carrying only display_until 2026-08-15 00:00 returns 422 the same way. A window whose display_until is before the injected clock returns 200. A successful window change writes exactly one movie.display_window_changed audit row whose before and after each hold exactly the keys display_from and display_until, and a request also changing the title writes a second row, movie.updated, holding exactly the key title. A window change on a film whose published_at is not null returns 200 and SELECT published_at is identical before and after.

Title: Grant and remove admin access by email from an admin-only Settings section
AcceptanceCriteria: An admin-only 'Admin access' section in Settings lists every granted email from an endpoint mounted under /api/admin, which returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED with no session and 403 FORBIDDEN with a customer or a manager session, refused by require_admin at the router (S-ADM-01); adding an email writes exactly one grant row and exactly one audit row, and removing one deletes that grant row and writes exactly one audit row, each in the same transaction as the change - with the audit insert forced to raise, the grant table's row count, every users.role and SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log are all unchanged (S-ADM-02); grants are stored and compared trimmed and case-insensitively: after granting ' Ada@Example.com ', a second add of 'ADA@example.com' leaves exactly one grant row, and POST /api/auth/register with 'ada@example.COM' returns 201 with role 'admin' and SELECT role FROM users WHERE lower(email)='ada@example.com' returns admin; a customer account that already exists when its email is granted still reads role 'customer' until it signs in, and POST /api/auth/login for it returns 200 with role 'admin', with SELECT role FROM users returning admin immediately after; a manager account whose email is granted becomes role 'admin' at its next sign-in, and SELECT count(*) FROM manager_screen_assignment for that user is identical before and after; a role in any request body is still ignored - POST /api/auth/register and POST /api/auth/login carrying "role":"admin" for an email that is not granted produce and keep role 'customer' (S-ACC-01); removing a granted email whose account is admin sets that account's role to 'customer' in the same transaction as the grant-row delete and its audit row, so the next request to GET /api/admin/movies with that account's unchanged cookie returns 403 FORBIDDEN (the role is read per request, S-XCT-10); an admin removing their own email receives a 4xx error envelope, and the grant row, SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log and their role are all unchanged; after a fresh seed the list holds 0 rows, and an add naming the seeded admin's email (admin-01@ at SEED_EMAIL_DOMAIN) receives a 4xx error envelope and writes no row, so the seeded admin is never on the list and cannot be demoted through it; sorted(member.value for member in Role) still equals ['admin', 'customer', 'guest', 'manager'] (S-SCP-06).
StatusNote: Every clause is asserted. The admin-only list is refused at the router. Each add and each removal writes one grant change and one audit row in one transaction, and a forced audit failure changes nothing. Emails are trimmed and case-insensitive. Register and next sign-in promote. A granted manager keeps its assignments. A body role is ignored. Removal demotes at once. Self-removal and the seeded admin are refused. The seeded admin_grant count is 0 (S-XCT-45 oracle). The roles stay four. The Settings section is covered by access.test.mjs.

AcceptanceCriteria: Seed one movie with published_at=2026-08-10T11:04:22+05:30, display_from=2026-08-14T00:00:00+05:30, display_until=2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30. With the clock injected: GET /api/movies returns it at T=2026-08-14T00:00:00+05:30 and at T=2026-08-20T23:59:59+05:30, and does not return it at T=2026-08-13T23:59:59+05:30 or at T=2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30 (4 assertions, exclusive upper bound); the same row with published_at NULL is absent at all four instants; the same row with display_from NULL, and again with display_until NULL, is absent at all four instants and str(stmt.compile()) for the listing query contains no occurrence of the substring 'COALESCE'; that same compiled string contains all three of 'published_at IS NOT NULL', 'display_from <=' and 'display_until >', and executing the statement directly at T=2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30 returns 0 rows, so the gate runs in the database and not in Python after the fetch; at an instant where it is excluded, GET /api/movies/{that id} returns 404 NOT_FOUND with a response body that, once error.request_id is deleted from each, is equal to the body of GET /api/movies/{an id that has never existed} - same error.code, same error.message, same error.details, and neither body carrying a key the other does not - while error.request_id is present on both and differs between them, because contract.json's conventions return a request id on EVERY error and two responses therefore never compare byte for byte; the anti-enumeration property this asserts is that an excluded film is indistinguishable from one that never existed, and the rendered copy is 'That movie is not showing.'; GET /api/movies/0 and GET /api/movies/abc return 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with the SQLAlchemy statement counter at 0 for the whole request; and at T=2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30 GET /api/movies/{id}/poster returns 302, GET /api/showtimes/{a showtime of that film} returns 200 and GET /api/showtimes/{that id}/seatmap returns 200 - the three ungated endpoints.
StatusNote: GET /api/movies/{id}/poster is now mounted (EP-BRW-03, S-BRW-18). Still open: no test asserts this story's clause that the poster returns 302 at T=2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30 for the excluded film. test_s_brw_01.py covers the showtime and seat-map halves only, and S-BRW-18's test uses a draft film, not the exclusive window bound. The rendered 'That movie is not showing.' is asserted in browse/render.test.mjs.
SourceRef: P-BRW-01 E1 S4 FR-ADR-021 FR-ADR-018 R-BRW-06

Title: Carry the six details a customer chooses between films on
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/movies returns each element with exactly the keys id, title, synopsis, runtime_minutes, certification, language, genres, poster_url, display_until and no others; certification and language are objects with exactly the keys id and name, and the string 'code' appears nowhere in the response body; genres is an array of {id, name} and is exactly [] for a movie with no movie_genre row, and that card's metadata row text then contains no genre name and no occurrence of 'unknown'; poster_url is string-equal to '/api/movies/{id}/poster' for every element, a full-string equality that admits no host of any kind; display_until is a string ending '+05:30' and is non-null on every element of the array; a movie whose poster object is missing from S3 still appears in the array and its card contains no img element, its poster box's text content is exactly the movie title (P-BRW-02 exception 1: the box draws the motif with the title inside it and no words are added), and the page text contains none of 'No poster', 'Image unavailable' or 'not found' (the box draws the perforation motif in --fr-poster-empty-mark with the title in --fr-ink-muted, COMPONENTS.md §3); and a synopsis of 900 characters is returned in full, with getComputedStyle on the card synopsis element reporting -webkit-line-clamp '3' and on the /movies/{id} synopsis element reporting 'none'.
StatusNote: needs a real browser: computed -webkit-line-clamp '3' on the card synopsis and 'none' on /movies/{id}, and the card of a film whose poster object is missing having no img (Poster.tsx removes it in onError, which only fires in a browser). The 390x844 screenshots do not show computed styles or the DOM.
SourceRef: P-BRW-02 E1 S4 SRC-001 §5.1.1 FR-ADR-021 R-BRW-02

Title: Order the listing newest first, by published_at descending with id descending as the tiebreak
AcceptanceCriteria: Seed A id=7 published_at=2026-08-12T10:00:00+05:30; B id=11 and C id=12 both published_at=2026-08-14T09:00:00+05:30; D id=13 published_at=NULL. GET /api/movies returns exactly the ids [12, 11, 7] in that order - 12 before 11 because published_at ties and id descends, 7 last because its published_at is two days earlier - and returns the identical order on 10 consecutive requests (the tiebreak is deterministic, not incidental); D is absent; GET /api/movies?sort=newest returns a body byte-identical to GET /api/movies; GET /api/movies?sort=title and ?sort=price return 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with the copy 'That sort option is not available.'; the sort parameter is typed as an Enum whose members are exactly ('newest',) (assert len(list(SortOption)) == 1) and str(stmt.compile()) for the listing contains no occurrence of the substring 'newest'; applying ?language_id={the language of A and C} returns [12, 7] - filtering narrows the set and does not reorder it; and the rendered listing contains no select element, no element with role 'listbox' or 'combobox', and no element whose accessible name contains 'Sort'.
SourceRef: P-BRW-03 E1 S4 FR-ADR-021 R-BRW-05

Title: Filter the listing by cinema, date, language and format, with one showtime satisfying every showtime filter at once
AcceptanceCriteria: Seed one visible film with exactly two showtimes: showtime 1 on 2026-08-17 in Hall 4 with format 2D, showtime 2 on 2026-08-18 in Hall 4 with format 3D (the two format labels are fixture values only and nothing here asserts a format vocabulary). GET /api/movies?date=2026-08-17 returns count 1; ?format_id={3D} returns count 1; ?date=2026-08-17&format_id={3D} returns count 0 with movies [] and the screen renders 'Nothing is showing for the chosen filters.' plus a control reading 'Clear filters'; GET /api/movies with no date returns count 1 (no date predicate is applied and it does not default to today); ?date=2026-08-14 compiles to the predicate starts_at >= 2026-08-13T18:30:00Z AND starts_at < 2026-08-14T18:30:00Z, so a showtime starting 23:45 local on 2026-08-14 is included and one starting 00:10 local on 2026-08-15 is not; the zone is read from the cinema row, not from a literal - reseeding cinema.timezone as 'Asia/Dubai' and repeating the same request compiles to starts_at >= 2026-08-13T20:00:00Z AND starts_at < 2026-08-14T20:00:00Z, and `rg -n 'Asia/Kolkata' backend/app/api backend/app/domain backend/app/models` returns hits only on lines carrying P-ADM-25's published sentence That is not a time zone this system recognises. Enter an IANA zone name, such as Asia/Kolkata.; ?date=14-08-2026 and ?date=2026-08-14T00:00:00 return 422 with 'That date is not valid.'; ?language_id=0 and ?format_id=abc return 422 with 'That filter is not valid.'; ?language_id=999999 (well-formed, no such row) returns 200 with count 0; and GET /api/movies?page=2 returns a body byte-identical to GET /api/movies.
StatusNote: The amended rg clause (hits only on lines carrying P-ADM-25's zone sentence) holds on current code: the only hit in backend/app/api, domain and models is domain/admin/cinemas.py:22, the ZONE_BAD sentence. But test_s_brw_04.py still runs the rg over this lane's files only, so no test asserts the clause as amended. The rest passes, and the empty state with 'Clear filters' is asserted in browse/render.test.mjs.
SourceRef: P-BRW-04 E1 S4 SRC-001 §5.1.3 FR-ADR-046 FR-ADR-018 R-BRW-03

Title: Serve the filter vocabularies as rows in use, and render a control only at two or more values
AcceptanceCriteria: Against the seeded catalogue (3 languages, 2 formats, 1 cinema, 2 certifications, 8 visible films, formats carried by showtimes): GET /api/reference returns languages length 3, formats length 2, cinemas length 1, certifications length 2, and no genres key; the listing then renders exactly one element whose accessible name is 'Language', exactly one whose accessible name is 'Format', and zero whose accessible name is 'Cinema'; reseed with 1 language and zero elements have the accessible name 'Language' and the page text contains no occurrence of the string 'Language'; a lookup row with is_active=false that a currently visible film still carries is present in its array and filtering by its id returns that film; a language row carried by no currently visible film is absent from the array; a format whose only showtime is past its sales cut-off is absent from formats; when GET /api/reference returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE while GET /api/movies returns 200, the listing renders every card, renders zero elements accessibly named 'Language', 'Format' or 'Cinema', still renders the date strip and 'Clear filters', a filter already present in the URL is still applied by the server, and the page text contains the string 'Filters are unavailable right now.' exactly once; and on day one with 0 languages and 0 formats the same three accessible names are absent and that string occurs 0 times.
SourceRef: P-BRW-04 E1 S4 E1 S6 FR-ADR-046 FR-ADR-010 R-BRW-03

Title: Bound the listing date strip at the day before the latest display_until in the filtered response
AcceptanceCriteria: With the clock injected at 2026-08-14T10:00:00+05:30 and a listing whose display_until values are 2026-08-19T00:00:00+05:30 and 2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30, the strip renders 'Any date' selected plus exactly 7 day buttons, 2026-08-14 through 2026-08-20 inclusive (max display_until is the 21st and the bound is exclusive, so the last day is the 20th and 14 to 20 is 7 days), and no button for 2026-08-21; applying a language filter that leaves only the film ending 2026-08-19 re-renders the strip with exactly 5 day buttons, 2026-08-14 through 2026-08-18; if 2026-08-20 was the selected day when that filter is applied, the selection returns to 'Any date', the next request carries no date parameter, and the polite live region announces 'The date filter was cleared. Nothing in this list is showing on that day.'; clearing filters restores the 7 buttons; when movies is [] the page contains no button whose accessible name is 'Any date' and no button whose accessible name matches '^(Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun) [0-9]{1,2} [A-Z][a-z]{2}$', in both empty states, and the empty-with-no-filters state renders 'Nothing is showing right now.' while the empty-with-filters state renders 'Nothing is showing for the chosen filters.' with 'Clear filters'; every day button's accessible name matches that same pattern, for example 'Sat 15 Aug' - 15 August 2026 is a SATURDAY; the neighbouring S-BRW-09 uses the same calendar correctly with 'Sun 16 Aug', and no button anywhere reads 'Today' or 'Tomorrow'; and pressing a day inside the range on which nothing is scheduled renders the ordinary 'Nothing is showing for the chosen filters.' state and returns 200, not an error status.
SourceRef: P-BRW-04 E1 S5 FR-ADR-018 R-BRW-03

Title: Let anyone browse the whole read path with no account
AcceptanceCriteria: With no cookie and no Authorization header: GET /api/movies, GET /api/movies/{id}, GET /api/movies/{id}/poster, GET /api/showtimes?movie_id={id}, GET /api/showtimes/{id}, GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap and GET /api/reference all return their success status (200, or 302 for the poster); a test walks app.routes, selects those seven paths, and asserts route.dependant.dependencies == [] for each - a read route in this epic carrying an auth dependency fails the test; the /seatmap response body for an anonymous caller and for a signed-in customer is byte-identical (compared as bytes on the same seeded showtime at the same injected instant); a guest rendering the seat map has zero cells whose accessible name ends 'held by you' and zero cells whose getComputedStyle border-width is '2px' (the held_by_me treatment is the only 2px border on the map, COMPONENTS.md §1.4), and the primary action reads exactly 'Sign in to hold these seats'; and a signed-in customer whose token has expired keeps receiving 200 from every read above, because the read path reads no token.
StatusNote: The poster route is now mounted, but test_s_brw_07.py leaves it out of READ_PATHS and _urls. The no-dependency walk and the anonymous 302 for /api/movies/{id}/poster are not asserted. Also needs a real browser: no seat cell with a computed border-width of 2px on a guest's map. The 'held by you' and 'Sign in to hold these seats' clauses are asserted in seatmap/render.test.mjs.
SourceRef: P-BRW-05 E1 S4 SRC-001 §4.1 FR-ADR-014 R-BRW-01

Title: List every showtime for a chosen movie and date in Asia/Kolkata
AcceptanceCriteria: Seed a visible movie with three showtimes on 2026-08-15 at 11:00, 14:30 and 19:30 local across two halls. GET /api/showtimes?movie_id={id}&date=2026-08-15 returns exactly 3 showtimes ordered by starts_at ASC then id ASC; each element carries exactly id, starts_at, ends_at, sales_close_at, sales_closed, screen{id,name}, cinema{id,name}, format ({id,name} or null) and base_price_paise; every instant string in the response ends '+05:30' and no instant in the response ends 'Z'; type(base_price_paise) is int for every element, which is False for a float and for a string; ends_at equals the stored column and is not starts_at plus runtime_minutes - assert with a showtime whose stored ends_at is 21:50 while starts_at 19:30 plus runtime_minutes 125 would give 21:35, and the response carries 21:50; with the injected clock at 2026-08-14T19:05:00Z (2026-08-15T00:35:00+05:30) and no date parameter, the response field date is '2026-08-15' and the returned showtimes are the 15th's; a movie failing either visibility gate returns 404 NOT_FOUND rendering 'That movie is not showing.' with a link reading 'Back to what is showing'; date=2026-8-15 returns 422 'That date is not valid.'; and a date with no showtimes returns 200 with an empty array rendering 'No showtimes on this date.'
SourceRef: P-BRW-06 E1 S4 SRC-001 §5.1.4 FR-ADR-018 R-BRW-04

Title: Name the next date the customer can actually buy on, or nothing at all
AcceptanceCriteria: Seed a visible movie with display_until=2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30 and showtimes: 2026-08-15 19:30 format 2D; 2026-08-16 11:00 format 3D only; 2026-08-17 09:00 format 2D (format labels are fixture values only). With SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES=+15 and the clock at 2026-08-15T21:00:00+05:30: GET /api/showtimes?movie_id={id}&date=2026-08-15 returns the 19:30 showtime with sales_closed true (19:30 plus 15 minutes is 19:45, which is before 21:00, and the list is NOT emptied) and next_date_with_showtimes '2026-08-16', and the screen renders the closed showtime plus a button reading 'Next: Sun 16 Aug'; the same request with format_id={2D} returns next_date_with_showtimes '2026-08-17', because the 16th's only showtime is 3D - proving conditions 3 and 4 are met by one showtime rather than by different ones; a request with date=2026-08-17 returns the 09:00 showtime and next_date_with_showtimes null, and the page contains no button whose accessible name starts 'Next: '; a request with date=2026-08-18, which has no showtime on or after it inside the display window, returns an empty list with next_date_with_showtimes null, the copy 'No showtimes for this movie.' renders, and the page contains no 'Next: ' button; a request with date=2026-08-19 compiles to a query whose upper bound parameter is that movie's display_until, equal to 2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30 (assert the bound parameter value, so the search cannot run past the display window); and with the clock at 2026-08-15T10:00:00+05:30, GET /api/showtimes?movie_id={id}&date=2026-08-15 returns the 19:30 showtime with sales_closed false and next_date_with_showtimes '2026-08-16', not '2026-08-15' - the requested date is excluded by the strictly-after condition even while it still holds an open showtime.
StatusNote: CR-002 B-6 resolved the doc defect: date=2026-08-17 returns the 09:00 showtime with next null, and the empty state moves to 2026-08-18. Still not asserted: the API test checks only next=null for the 17th, not that the 09:00 showtime is returned. No API test covers date=2026-08-18 (empty list, next null). No render covers the 17th showing no 'Next: ' button. The 18th's empty-state render is asserted.
SourceRef: P-BRW-06 P-BRW-07 E1 S4 E1 S6 R-BRW-04

Title: Show a closed showtime, marked closed, rather than hiding it
AcceptanceCriteria: With SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES=+15 and a showtime at starts_at=2026-08-14T19:30:00+05:30: the response carries sales_close_at '2026-08-14T19:45:00+05:30' (19:30 plus 15 minutes); at injected T=2026-08-14T19:44:59+05:30 sales_closed is false and at T=2026-08-14T19:45:00+05:30 sales_closed is true (the boundary instant is closed); with SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES=-15 and no other change the same showtime carries sales_close_at '2026-08-14T19:15:00+05:30' (19:30 minus 15 minutes) and sales_closed true at T=19:20:00+05:30 - a reversal of OPEN-BOOK-03 is this one configured value and no code change; SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name='showtime' AND column_name='sales_close_at' returns 0 after every migration has run; with SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES set to 'fifteen' the process exits non-zero at boot with stderr containing the string 'SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES' and does not start with an effective value of 15, and with it unset the process boots with the S7.9 default of +15; a closed showtime button renders the word 'Closed', carries tabindex='-1' and aria-disabled='true', is not reached by pressing Tab from the showtime button before it, leaves window.location.pathname unchanged when clicked, and its accessible name ends 'sales closed'; opening /showtimes/{id} for a closed showtime returns the full seat map with every seat unselectable and the banner exactly 'Sales for this showtime have closed.'; and `rg -o 'Sales for this showtime have closed\.' frontend/src | wc -l` returns exactly 1.
StatusNote: The unset half of the config conflict was amended on 2026-10-18 (unset boots with +15), but no test boots with SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES unset and asserts +15. Every test passes '15' explicitly. Still a cell/code conflict: the cell says the 'fifteen' refusal goes to stderr, but the boot refusal is a JSON line on stdout by design (SRC-002 7.6, app/__main__.py), and the test asserts stdout. The render clauses are asserted.
SourceRef: P-BRW-07 E1 S4 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-03 FR-ADR-042 R-BRW-04

Title: Serve the seat map as the real layout of the hall, scoped to this showtime's frozen seat set
AcceptanceCriteria: For a seeded showtime in a hall whose seat set has 220 seats with max(gr)=12 and max(gc)=22: GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap returns screen.rows 12 and screen.cols 22; seats has length 220 and is ordered gr ASC then gc ASC, so the seat labelled A-2 precedes A-12 in the array; a seat carries row 'C', num 12, gr 3 and gc 14 as four separate fields; seats contains no object at any (gr, gc) the seeded hall records as an aisle, and the string 'blocked' does not appear anywhere in the response body; the showtime object on this response has exactly the keys id, starts_at, sales_close_at, sales_closed; every seat carries is_active as a boolean, and a seat object constructed without it raises ValidationError at response-model construction rather than serialising; adding a seat to the hall after the showtime was created leaves this showtime's screen.cols at 22 and the new seat absent from seats; retiring one seat returns it with is_active false and its state field unchanged; retiring all 220 returns 200 with 220 seats and is_active false on every one, and the screen renders 220 cells, every accessible name ending 'out of service', none activating on Enter or Space, and the banner exactly 'None of the seats in this hall are available.' (the cell treatment itself is asserted in S-BRW-12); a showtime whose seat set has zero rows returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR rendering 'The seat map could not be loaded.' plus a request id matching the id in the JSON log line for that request; showtime id 999999 returns 404 'That showtime could not be found.'; and /seatmap for a non-integer id returns 422 with the SQLAlchemy statement counter at 0.
StatusNote: One clause is open: 'none activating on Enter or Space' on the 220 out-of-service cells. The SSR render harness (renderToStaticMarkup) cannot dispatch a keydown, so this needs a real browser. Every other clause passes.
SourceRef: P-BRW-08 E1 S4 E1 S6 SRC-001 §5.2.1 FR-ADR-016 R-SEAT-01 R-SEAT-07

Title: Serve three objective seat states and let the client compute the fourth
AcceptanceCriteria: For showtime 812 with a booking row for (812, C-12), a live Redis lock for (812, C-13) and nothing for C-14: GET /api/showtimes/812/seatmap returns state 'sold' for C-12, 'held' for C-13 and 'available' for C-14, and a fourth value raises ValidationError at response-model construction; two callers with different sessions receive byte-identical bodies for the same request, both issued while the C-13 lock is still live because the fixture creates that lock with a 300-second TTL - real Redis expires on its own clock and the injected application clock does not move it - and the seatmap body carries no key whose name contains 'expires', 'ttl', 'remaining', 'session' or 'request', so nothing in it is free to differ between two viewers or two calls; a client holding a hold token containing C-13 renders exactly one cell whose accessible name ends 'held by you' and a client with no token renders zero; a fixture rendering one cell in each of the four states produces four distinct values of the cell's data-glyph attribute, exactly the set {outline, bar, hatch, check} (COMPONENTS.md §1.4), and with a test stylesheet forcing every --fr-seat-* fill and ink token to the same colour those four values are still four and still distinct, so no state is carried by colour alone; a seat with is_active false reports getComputedStyle border-style 'dashed', border-width '1px' and background-color 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)', renders its seat number, receives focus when ArrowRight is pressed on the cell at the gc to its left, has the accessible name 'Row C seat 12, Premium, out of service', and fires no selection on Enter or Space in any state including sold; the legend renders 5 swatches and the fifth reads 'Out of service'; when every seat is sold the full 220-cell grid renders plus the banner 'Every seat for this showtime is sold.' and the page text contains no occurrence of 'Nothing'; and a seat that changes state between two polls carries a 2px --fr-focus-ring outline for --fr-motion-change and no longer carries it once that duration has elapsed on the fake timer, while under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the same element reports getComputedStyle animation-name 'none' and still carries the outline for the same duration.
StatusNote: needs a real browser: computed border-style dashed, 1px and a transparent background on an inactive seat; the four glyphs under a one-colour stylesheet; ArrowRight focus movement; Enter/Space firing no selection; the change ring on a fake timer and under prefers-reduced-motion. The glyph set, the names, the legend and the sold-out banner are asserted in seatmap/render.test.mjs.
SourceRef: P-BRW-09 E1 S4 SRC-001 §5.2.2 FR-ADR-045 FR-ADR-030 R-SEAT-01 R-SEAT-06

Title: Send the category and the already-rounded price of every seat
AcceptanceCriteria: With base_price_paise=24999 and categories at 0, 1250 and 3333 basis points, GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap returns categories price_paise of exactly 24999, 28124 and 33331: 24999*10000+5000 = 249995000, //10000 = 24999; 24999*11250+5000 = 281243750, //10000 = 28124, rounding UP from an exact 28123.875; 24999*13333+5000 = 333316667, //10000 = 33331, rounding DOWN from an exact 33331.1667; every seat carries a price_paise identical to its own category's value in the same response (assert across all 220 seats); the implementation computes (base_price_paise * (10000 + uplift_basis_points) + 5000) // 10000, type(price_paise) is int for every category and every seat in the response (which is False for a bool and for a float), and `rg -n 'float| / ' backend/app/domain/pricing.py` returns 0 hits because the formula uses // and never true division; three seats of the 3333 bp category sum to 3 * 33331 = 99993 and the response's own total is 99993, not re-rounded to 99990 or 100000; the legend renders one row per category reading 'Premium  $281.24' for the 28124 case; the seat map page text contains none of 'Tax', 'Booking fee', 'Convenience' or 'Discount'; a category whose price has not yet arrived renders a --fr-surface-inset block in its legend row (COMPONENTS.md §3) whose text contains no '$' character, and the page text contains no occurrence of '$0.00'; and the raw JSON payload contains no '$' character and matches the regular expression '[0-9]+\.[0-9]' nowhere.
StatusNote: needs a real browser: the computed --fr-surface-inset fill of the legend's price placeholder. The prices, the rounding, the 'Premium  $281.24' row, the no-$ placeholder, the no-$0.00 rule and the sweeps are asserted (USD amendment).
SourceRef: P-BRW-10 E1 S4 SRC-001 §5.2.3 FR-ADR-038 FR-ADR-036 R-SEAT-03

Title: Derive the category bands from the payload and say what happens when they interleave
AcceptanceCriteria: For a 6-row hall where gr 1, 2 and 4 are all category 1, gr 3 holds no seats, gr 5 holds both categories and gr 6 is all category 2: the derivation function returns exactly two bands, [(category 1, gr 1, gr 4), (category 2, gr 6, gr 6)] - gr 3 is void and does not break the run, gr 5 is mixed and does; the screen contains 0 elements carrying the data-band-rule attribute (the dashed --fr-rule drawn only between two adjacent bands, COMPONENTS.md §1.5), because the mixed gr 5 sits between them; categories is returned as [{id:1},{id:2}] ordered by the lowest gr of first appearance with id ascending as the tiebreak, and the legend rows render in that same top-to-bottom order; given a stubbed payload whose categories array is [{id:9},{id:3}] the legend renders the id 9 row above the id 3 row, so the client preserves payload order and applies no ordering of its own; a category appearing in two separate runs yields 2 entries from the derivation function and exactly 1 legend row for that category; when every grid row is mixed the DOM contains 0 elements carrying data-band-rule and 0 carrying data-band, and exactly one element renders the text 'Seat categories are mixed within rows. Each seat's category is in the legend and in its label.'; a category with no seat in this showtime's seat set is absent from categories; two seats sharing a gr with different row strings returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with a request id and no seatmap body; and retiring one seat of gr 2 leaves the derivation function's output unchanged, still exactly [(category 1, gr 1, gr 4), (category 2, gr 6, gr 6)], so a retired seat still participates in its band.
SourceRef: P-BRW-16 E1 S4 FR-ADR-016 FR-ADR-051 FR-ADR-072 R-SEAT-03

Title: Refresh the seat map on the interval the server publishes, and pause it when nobody is looking
AcceptanceCriteria: With poll_interval_seconds=3 in the payload and a fake client timer: exactly one GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap is issued per 3 seconds of client time; with a response that takes 5 seconds, no second request is issued until the first lands and the interval then restarts (at most one in flight); with document.hidden true no request is issued for 30 seconds of client time, and the visibilitychange to visible fires one request immediately; the rendered screen contains no refresh or reload control; a poll that fails with a network error or a 5xx leaves the previously rendered grid unchanged in the DOM and adds exactly one strip reading 'The seat map is not updating. The seats shown may be out of date.', and a second consecutive failure leaves the map still on screen; the server rejects a non-integer SEATMAP_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS at boot with a non-zero exit and boots with the S7.9 default of 3 when it is missing; and with SEATMAP_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS=5 the payload reports 5 and the client issues one request per 5 seconds with no frontend redeploy, which is what proves the client holds no interval constant of its own.
StatusNote: Done 2026-11-07: every clause asserted and passing; see evidence/README.md.
SourceRef: P-BRW-11 E1 S4 E1 S6 SRC-002 §8.6.1 FR-ADR-045 R-SEAT-06

Title: Cache the read path, invalidate the listings by a generation counter, and keep browsing alive when Redis is gone
AcceptanceCriteria: A listing read reads cache:listing:generation and writes cache:listing:{generation}:{fingerprint} with a TTL of 60 seconds; a seat map read writes cache:seatmap:{showtime_id} with a TTL of 10 seconds (assert both by issuing TTL on the key and reading 60 and 10); after an admin publish commits, cache:listing:generation has increased by exactly 1 and the next listing read returns the new film; the harness records every Redis command issued during one admin publish plus one listing read (a recording client wrapper, or MONITOR), and that log contains exactly one command matching '^INCR cache:listing:generation$', at least one matching '^SETEX cache:listing:', 0 matching '^SET cache:listing:', 0 matching '^SCAN' and 0 matching '^(SET|DEL) cache:listing:generation'; a booking commit issues DEL cache:seatmap:{id}; with the DEL forced to raise, the transaction still commits, the recorded command log contains exactly one DEL for that key, one WARNING log line carries the write's request id, and TTL on the key returns -2 within 10 seconds; on a cache miss with 5 concurrent callers exactly one SET cache:seatmap:{id}:rebuild with NX PX 2000 succeeds, and each of the 4 losers re-reads the key once, finds it empty, and issues its own PostgreSQL seat-map query (assert 4 such queries on the statement counter and every request completing inside the 2000 ms lock TTL); with the counter key deleted, the next INCR yields 1 and the read succeeds; and with Redis stopped, GET /api/movies and GET /api/showtimes both return 200 with bodies byte-identical to the same two requests issued with Redis running against the same seeded catalogue at the same injected instant - the instant is pinned because sales_closed and the defaulted date field are derived from the clock at read time and would otherwise be free to differ between the two runs for reasons that have nothing to do with the cache - and the rendered page text contains no occurrence of 'unavailable' or 'not updating'.
StatusNote: The code is now wired: the admin film publish/unpublish calls bump_listing_generation (api/admin/movies.py), and a booking commit DELs cache:seatmap (asserted by test_s_pay_07). test_s_brw_16.py still does not assert two clauses. (1) An admin publish raises cache:listing:generation by exactly 1, with the one-INCR command log over a publish plus a listing read. (2) A booking commit whose DEL is forced to raise still commits. The page-text sweep is asserted in browse/render.test.mjs:167.
SourceRef: P-BRW-12 E1 S4 SRC-002 §8.2.1 FR-ADR-030 FR-ADR-028 R-QLY-04 R-SEAT-06

Title: Serve posters from our own bucket by redirect, and never hotlink
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/movies/11/poster returns 302 with Content-Length 0 and a Location header whose host is the configured bucket host and whose query string carries both X-Amz-Expires=3600 and X-Amz-Signature; the Cache-Control header is max-age=300 from POSTER_REDIRECT_CACHE_SECONDS, and with that variable set to 3600 or 4000 the process exits non-zero at boot with stderr containing the string 'POSTER_REDIRECT_CACHE_SECONDS' (the assertion is strictly less than the 3600-second presign expiry, so a cached redirect cannot outlive its target); a movie whose poster_object_key is NULL returns 404 NOT_FOUND and its card contains no img element, its card text content is exactly the movie title, and the page text contains none of 'No poster', 'Image unavailable' or 'not found'; a movie id that does not exist returns 404 whose body, once error.request_id is deleted from each, is equal to that 404's body on error.code, error.message and error.details, with error.request_id present on both and differing; appending ?key=../../etc/passwd returns 302 whose Location, split with urlsplit, has a path equal to the path of the Location returned for the same request without that parameter, and that path's object-key component is string-equal to that movie row's poster_object_key, while the whole Location contains no occurrence of 'etc/passwd' and none of '..' - only the path is compared and the query string is deliberately excluded from the comparison, because a correct implementation presigns every request independently, so X-Amz-Date, X-Amz-Signature and X-Amz-Credential all differ between two calls made in different seconds with no bug present and a byte comparison of the whole header would pass only by landing in the same second; with every outbound socket connection blocked at the transport layer the handler still returns 302 and its Location carries the configured bucket host, the same path as the unblocked call and a query string containing both X-Amz-Signature and X-Amz-Expires=3600, because presigning is a local HMAC and issues no network call; and a movie that is unpublished or outside its display window still returns 302 here, which is the ungated behaviour of record.
StatusNote: Built: GET /api/movies/{id}/poster is a 302 to a presigned GET signed offline by botocore (the SDK blocker is gone). test_s_brw_18.py asserts the 302, Content-Length 0, the bucket host, X-Amz-Expires=3600, the signature, max-age=300, and 404 NOT_FOUND for a null key and an unknown id. Not yet asserted: (1) the boot refusal at POSTER_REDIRECT_CACHE_SECONDS 3600 and 4000 (no test names the variable); (2) the 404 body equality with request ids differing; (3) the ?key=../../etc/passwd path comparison; (4) the 302 with outbound sockets blocked; (5) a film outside its display window (a draft is covered); (6) the card's no-img, title-only render.
SourceRef: P-BRW-15 E1 S4 SRC-002 §10.6.3 FR-ADR-061 R-BRW-02

Title: Rate limit the seat map per address, split the two 429 states, and fail closed when Redis is gone
AcceptanceCriteria: The 121st request within one minute from one address to GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with a Retry-After header, and requests 1 to 120 return 200; the limiter is one counter per address, created by INCR with a 60-second expiry set when the counter is created, so a window opens on that address's first request; starting from a deleted counter key, seven simulated viewers polling that endpoint every 3 seconds from one address for 60 seconds of real time send 7 * 20 = 140 requests (60/3 = 20 each) into that one shared counter, and exactly 120 return 200 and exactly 20 return 429 - the count is what is asserted and no assertion names which viewer is refused, because with seven concurrent pollers the budget is spent by the second request of the 18th round (17 * 7 = 119 sent, the 120th succeeds and the 121st is the first refusal) and nothing in the specification fixes which viewer sends it; every one of those 20 refusals carries a Retry-After header whose value parses as an integer in 1..60, and the window is measured in real time because the counter and its expiry live in Redis, which honours its own clock and not the injected application clock; a 429 on a poll while a map is on screen leaves the last good map unchanged in the DOM, renders 'Too many requests. The seat map will update again shortly.' and, on the fake timer, issues no request at Retry-After minus 1 second and exactly one at Retry-After; a 429 on the first load, with no map and no poll loop, renders 'The seat map could not be loaded.' with a control reading 'Try again' and the page text contains no occurrence of 'will update again shortly'; with Redis unreachable, GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE rendering exactly 'The seat map is unavailable right now. You can still browse showtimes. Try again in a few minutes.' and `rg -o 'The seat map is unavailable right now\.' frontend/src | wc -l` returns exactly 1; and in the same condition GET /api/movies and GET /api/showtimes both return 200, because neither is a limited endpoint.
StatusNote: Unchanged doc defect, with no amendment: the cell describes an INCR fixed-window counter, with seven pollers over 60 real seconds giving exactly 120/20. PRD S7.4 specifies one token-bucket limiter, which refills continuously. The PRD outranks the Bible, so this needs a cell amendment or a ruling. Also not asserted: the 'Too many requests. The seat map will update again shortly.' strip on a poll 429, with the last good map kept. The 121st request answering 429, the Redis-down 503, the first-load 429 and the Retry-After wait are asserted.
SourceRef: P-BRW-11 P-BRW-12 E1 S4 E1 S6 FR-ADR-058 FR-ADR-028 R-QLY-04

every money column on booking, booking_seat and payment is bigint with a name ending in _paise - SELECT column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name IN ('booking','booking_seat','payment') AND column_name LIKE '%paise%' returns exactly total_paise, price_paise, base_price_paise_applied, amount_paise and every data_type is bigint; rg -n 'float\(|Decimal' backend/app/domain/pricing.py backend/app/api/bookings.py returns 0 hits; 275.00 dollars is stored and returned as the integer 27500 and 1,661.46 dollars as 166146 - each is the dollar figure multiplied by the ratio 100; for the five-seat fixture of S-PAY-02 (three seats at 30938 paise and two at 36666 paise, 3 x 30938 + 2 x 36666 = 166146) the 201 body of POST /api/bookings carries total_paise as the JSON number 166146, every seats[].price_paise and seats[].base_price_paise_applied is a JSON number and not a string, the body carries no key named total, amount, price, total_formatted or currency_display, and the raw response text contains no dollar sign; the API and domain layers format no money at all - rg -nP '\$(\{|\d)' backend/app/api backend/app/domain returns 0 hits (a dollar sign before a digit or an interpolation; a regex end anchor is not a currency sign), so the only formatted figure in the product is produced in frontend/src at render time; Title: Compute every seat price and every total with one integer half-up function
AcceptanceCriteria: seat_price_paise(base_price_paise, uplift_basis_points) returns base plus the half-up rounding of base x uplift / 10000, in whole paise: seat_price_paise(27500, 1250) returns 30938 (27500 x 1250 / 10000 = 3437.5, half-up 3438), seat_price_paise(27500, 3333) returns 36666 (9165.75 rounds to 9166), seat_price_paise(27500, 0) returns 27500, and seat_price_paise(25000, 3333) returns 33333 (8332.5 rounds to 8333) - the case where half-even would return 33332; seat_price_paise(27500.0, 1250) and seat_price_paise(27500, 1250.0) each raise TypeError rather than rounding the float, and seat_price_paise(-1, 1250) and seat_price_paise(27500, -1) each raise ValueError; exactly one implementation of the formula exists - rg -n 'def seat_price_paise' backend/app backend/migrations returns exactly 1 hit and it is in backend/app/domain/pricing.py, and rg -n 'def .*price.*paise' backend/app --glob '!**/pricing.py' returns 0 hits; the total is the arithmetic sum of the already-rounded per-seat prices and is never itself rounded - for three seats at 30938 and two at 36666 the total is exactly 3 x 30938 + 2 x 36666 = 166146, and a test asserts the returned total equals 166146 and does not equal 166144, the figure produced by carrying exact values and rounding once at the end (3 x 30937.5 + 2 x 36665.75 = 166144.0); the basis-point denominator and the half constant are named constants defined once - rg -n 'BASIS_POINTS_DENOMINATOR|ROUNDING_HALF_NUMERATOR' backend/app returns their definitions only in backend/app/domain/pricing.py - and rg -n '\b10000\b|\b5000\b' backend/app/domain backend/app/api backend/app/workers --glob '!**/pricing.py' | rg -v '^\S+:\d+:\s*[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*_(MS|SECONDS)\s*=\s*\d+\s*(#.*)?$' returns 0 hits - a hit is excused only when it is a whole-line assignment of a named duration constant whose name ends _MS or _SECONDS, and every other bare 10000 or 5000, in any expression, is a hit; rg -n 'uplift_basis_points\s*[-+*/]|[-+*/]\s*uplift_basis_points' backend/app --glob '!**/pricing.py' returns 0 hits, so no caller anywhere does its own uplift arithmetic; the pricing test supplies 27500 and the uplifts 0, 1250 and 3333 as literals and reads no seed data - rg -n 'seed|session|db_|client\.' over the pricing test module returns 0 hits - because the category names and uplifts are ASSUMED under SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-01 and are illustrative only
StatusNote: Every clause is asserted and passes. The 10000|5000 sweep now excuses only a whole-line *_MS / *_SECONDS duration constant (CR-002 A-1), so the mutex-TTL blocker is resolved.

AcceptanceCriteria: With SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=180 the computed bound is 180 x 1000 / 10 = 18000 ms: PAYMENT_SIMULATED_DELAY_MS=1500 boots, 17999 boots, 18000 exits non-zero before binding a port with a message naming the variable, the configured value and the computed bound, 60000 exits the same way, and 0 exits the same way; the bound follows the TTL rather than being a literal - with SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=60 the bound is 6000, 5999 boots and 6000 exits non-zero; PAYMENT_PROVIDER unset exits non-zero, which is the proof that no default and no fallback to simulated exists, and PAYMENT_PROVIDER=stripe exits non-zero with a message stating that no other provider exists; PAYMENT_SIMULATOR_FAIL_KEY_PREFIX=a exits non-zero and =deadbeef exits non-zero, each with a message naming the variable, the value and the reason - both are drawn entirely from [0-9a-f-] and a browser-minted Idempotency-Key could begin with them by chance; FAIL_ boots; unset exits non-zero and a 33-character value exits non-zero; on a successful boot stdout carries exactly one JSON line whose payment_provider field reads simulated, and GET /health/ready returns a body whose payment_provider field reads simulated; the delay 1500 and the prefix FAIL_ are ASSUMED - no source names either - so both are read from the settings module and appear as a literal nowhere else: rg -n "\b1500\b|[\"']FAIL_" backend/app --glob '!**/config.py' --glob '!**/settings.py' returns 0 hits - the pattern matches FAIL_ only where it opens a quoted string literal, because the S7.9 variable name PAYMENT_SIMULATOR_FAIL_KEY_PREFIX itself contains FAIL_ and every module that reads the setting names it

Title: Run the confirm transaction in the specified order and recover from a crash at every step
AcceptanceCriteria: An instrumented confirm records its steps in exactly this order: idempotency insert, hold re-validation in Redis, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the showtime row, showtime read, price sum from the hold snapshot, payment capture, booking and booking_seat insert, audit no-op, receipt_dispatch insert, outbox_message insert, idempotency record completed, COMMIT - then, after the commit, Redis lock release with the compare-and-delete script plus removal of the token from holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:{showtime_id}, DEL cache:seatmap:7, and the bounded queue send; SELECT ... FOR UPDATE is taken only on the showtime row and never to test whether a seat is free - rg -n 'FOR UPDATE' backend/app/api/bookings.py returns exactly 1 hit and that line also matches 'showtime', and the S-XCT-03 allow-list holds; step 9 writes receipt_dispatch with dispatch_seq 1, status pending, attempts 0 and every timestamp null, and no committed state exists in which an outbox_message row exists without its receipt_dispatch row - after 50 confirms, SELECT count(*) FROM outbox_message o WHERE o.topic='receipt.send' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM receipt_dispatch r WHERE r.booking_id = (o.payload->>'booking_id')::bigint AND r.dispatch_seq = (o.payload->>'dispatch_seq')::int) returns 0; a fault injected between the capture and the booking insert leaves SELECT count(*) FROM payment, FROM booking and FROM idempotency_record all at 0, and a retry with the same key then produces exactly one payment and exactly one booking; a fault injected after COMMIT but before the response leaves the booking, its seats, the payment, the pending receipt_dispatch, the outbox row and a completed idempotency record, and the retry with the same key replays the stored response byte-for-byte while SELECT count(*) FROM booking stays at 1; the sales cut-off is not enforced here - a confirm on a showtime whose cut-off has passed returns 201, and rg -n 'SALES_CLOSED' backend/app/api/bookings.py returns 0 hits; the 201 is emitted only after the queue send returns, fails or times out at QUEUE_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS=2000 - with a stubbed queue that never answers the response is still 201, the outbox row is still pending, and rg -n 'BackgroundTasks|create_task' backend/app/api/bookings.py returns 0 hits; booking.total_paise equals SELECT sum(price_paise) FROM booking_seat WHERE booking_id = the new id and SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE booking_id = the new id equals the number of seats in the hold, or the transaction rolls back with 500 INTERNAL_ERROR and SELECT count(*) FROM booking is unchanged
StatusNote: Every clause is asserted and passes. The seat FOR UPDATE sweep is replaced by the S-XCT-03 allow-list (CR-002 A-2), so the admin screen-lock blocker is resolved.

Title: Treat a unique-constraint violation as the guard working
AcceptanceCriteria: With two live holders of one seat on showtime 7 both confirming, one gets 201 and the other gets 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE whose details.unavailable_seats is exactly ['F7'], and SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=7 AND seat_id=402 returns 1; Title: Resolve the caller's role and screen scope once, on the reports router
AcceptanceCriteria: The reports router is mounted with one role dependency admitting exactly manager and admin plus a report_scope dependency, asserted by reading [d.dependency.__name__ for d in reports_router.dependencies] and finding exactly those two names in that order; an unauthenticated GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=day returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED with 'Sign in to see the dashboard.'; the same request as a customer and as a guest returns 403 FORBIDDEN with 'This page is for managers and administrators.'; the hold's token is added to `holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:{showtime_id}` and each key to `instance:{instance_id}:holds`, both with the hold's TTL, asserted by SMEMBERS and TTL; `DEL cache:seatmap:77` is issued after the Redis lock writes and never before, asserted by command ordering in the log; Title: Decide expiry by asking Redis, never by comparing clocks
AcceptanceCriteria: With a hold acquired at 2026-08-14T14:02:37.412Z and SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=180, so expires_at is 2026-08-14T14:05:37.412Z: while all of the hold's keys are present a confirm returns 201; when the hold's keys are gone the same request returns 409 with error.code HOLD_EXPIRED, asserted twice over the two ways the keys actually go - once with the test deleting them directly, and once with the hold acquired under SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=2 and the test polling `EXISTS lock:seat:77:402` until it returns 0 so that Redis's own TTL removed them; and - this is the assertion that proves the server compares no clocks - advancing the INJECTED APPLICATION CLOCK to exactly expires_at and then to expires_at plus 1s while the keys are still present returns 201 and never 409 HOLD_EXPIRED, because real Redis honours its own TTL and knows nothing about the injected clock, so a criterion asserting HOLD_EXPIRED at that instant would fail against a correct implementation; no test reads the wall clock, asserted by `rg -n 'datetime\.now\(|datetime\.utcnow\(|datetime\.today\(|date\.today\(|time\.time\(|time\.time_ns\(' backend/tests/` returning 0 hits, and every `time.sleep(` under `backend/tests/` sits inside a loop that polls an external process or Redis (an HTTP readiness probe, a container, a database transaction, or an `EXISTS`) and that loop is bounded by an iteration count rather than by a clock reading, asserted by a test that parses each hit's enclosing `for`/`while` with `ast` and finds a bounded `range(...)` or counter; the liveness function takes no clock argument, asserted by inspect.signature listing no parameter named now, clock, at or instant and no parameter annotated datetime, and it performs no comparison against expires_at, asserted by the Redis command log for one liveness check containing exactly one GET of the hold's key and no other command; GET /api/holds/{hold_token} with a well-formed 43-character token matching no key returns 409 HOLD_EXPIRED with `The hold on your seats has ended and they have been released. You have not been charged. Choose them again if they are still free.`; with a key present whose value is a different token it returns 403 HOLD_NOT_OWNED with the same sentence; with a token of 42 characters, of 44 characters, or of 43 characters containing `+`, `/` or `=`, it returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID with `This request could not be processed. Return to the seat map and choose your seats again.` and the Redis command log for that request is empty; a client whose clock is one minute slow still succeeds while the key lives, and one whose clock is fast is still accepted - both asserted by the server's answer being independent of any client-supplied instant, and by GET /api/holds/{hold_token} taking no query parameter and no request body at all, asserted against the EP-HLD-02 contract entry whose request query and body objects are both empty.
StatusNote: The wall-clock and sleep sweep now passes under the amended cell (CR-002 A-5): rg plus an ast check of each bounded poll loop. It is two path segments and reaches no route (404), the test only reports it, and the code fix approved in CR-002 B-13 / Q-R3-05 has not been made.

The constraint is restored, the repeat produces exactly 1 row again, and SELECT conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'booking_seat'::regclass AND contype = 'u' returns exactly one row whose definition is UNIQUE (showtime_id, seat_id) with no WHERE clause. Stage A - which is S-XCT-01's separate fifty-request run against the HOLD endpoint, not any part of this story - produces one winner even with the constraint dropped, and that is the expected result and not a finding, because at the hold endpoint the Redis lock decides and the constraint is never reached. The script refuses to run when --base-url does not resolve to a loopback address, exiting non-zero with LOCAL ONLY; each stage prints one JSON object on stdout carrying operator (from STRESS_OPERATOR, no default, exit non-zero when unset), run_at, stage and every count above.

Title: Take the real client address from the right of X-Forwarded-For
AcceptanceCriteria: The limiter keys on the address the load balancer reports and not on the load balancer itself, proved as its own test rather than inferred from the limiter's tests passing. With RATE_LIMIT_HOLD_IP_PER_MIN=2 and the local proxy configured to append the peer address to X-Forwarded-For exactly as an ALB does, three POST /api/showtimes/41/holds requests arrive from one simulated client 198.51.100.77 for three different seats: the first carries X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.9 and reaches the application as '203.0.113.9, 198.51.100.77', the second carries X-Forwarded-For: 192.0.2.5 and reaches it as '192.0.2.5, 198.51.100.77', and the third carries no such header and reaches it as '198.51.100.77'. The first two return 201 and the third returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with header Retry-After: 30 and body message 'Too many attempts. Try again in 30 seconds.' - all three were counted in one bucket, and two forged leftmost values changed nothing. Against an implementation that trusts the leftmost entry the third request returns 201 and the test fails. The resolved address is 198.51.100.77 in all three cases, read back from the request log line's client_ip field. The application runs with --proxy-headers and an explicit --forwarded-allow-ips, asserted by rg -n 'proxy-headers' and rg -n 'forwarded-allow-ips' over the entrypoint returning one hit each, and FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS = * exits non-zero at boot naming the variable. Title: Cache the seat map and the listings cache-aside, invalidating with DEL after commit
AcceptanceCriteria: The seat map is cached at cache:seatmap:{showtime_id} with SEATMAP_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (10) and the listings at their own key with LISTING_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (60), asserted by reading TTL cache:seatmap:41 immediately after a miss and finding a value between 1 and 10 inclusive - never -1 or -2, which Redis returns for a key with no expiry and for a key that does not exist, and which would let a build that never creates the key pass at all; after a hold, a release or a booking commits, EXISTS cache:seatmap:41 returns 0 immediately after the response - the entry is deleted and never replaced with a computed value, which is what distinguishes a DEL from a SET; a recording Redis client asserts the command order for one hold is SET lock:seat:41:312 NX, then the transaction COMMIT, then EVAL of the compare-and-delete script on the lock key (never a bare DEL of a lock: key), then DEL cache:seatmap:41, in that order and no other, and the recorder is not reset between the SET NX and the COMMIT, so SET NX < COMMIT is asserted too; a rebuild acquires cache:seatmap:41:rebuild with SET NX PX CACHE_REBUILD_LOCK_TTL_MS (default 2000, read from configuration and asserted by rg -n '2000' backend/app/core/cache.py returning 0 hits), and a caller that does not get the lock waits for at most CACHE_REBUILD_LOCK_TTL_MS, re-reads the cache, and on a second miss reads PostgreSQL directly rather than blocking, asserted by two concurrent misses both returning 200 whose seats arrays are equal element for element and in the same order - the comparison is on the seat states and not on the whole body, which may carry a per-response generated instant - and exactly one of them issuing the rebuild query; a DEL that raises is neither retried nor rolled back, asserted by patching it to raise and observing the booking still committed and the entry gone within 10 s; rg -F 'stampede' backend/app/core/cache.py returns at least one hit, so the site carries the comment naming the scenario; worst-case staleness a customer can see is 10 s cache TTL plus 3 s poll interval = 13 s, asserted against real Redis in real elapsed time rather than against the injected clock, because Redis expires its own keys on its own clock and advancing the application's clock leaves the cache entry in place: a seat is released and a poll reports it available no more than 13 s of real elapsed time after the release; a stale map never causes an oversell, which S-XCT-01's gate asserts.

Title: Behave differently for each of Redis's three jobs when Redis is gone
AcceptanceCriteria: With the Redis container stopped: POST /api/showtimes/41/holds returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE on the configured client timeout with message 'Seat holds are unavailable right now. You can still browse showtimes. Try again in a few minutes.', and POST /api/bookings returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE with message 'We cannot complete your booking right now. You have not been charged. Try again in a few minutes. If you need help, quote {request_id}.' (P-HLD-14, CONFIRM_REDIS_DOWN), with SELECT count(*) FROM payment unchanged; GET /api/movies and GET /api/showtimes return 200 served from PostgreSQL, because they are not rate-limited; GET /api/showtimes/41/seatmap returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and not 200, because it is rate-limited, the limiter runs before the cache and it fails closed, and its message is exactly 'The seat map is unavailable right now. You can still browse showtimes. Try again in a few minutes.' (P-BRW-12, which owns that code on that endpoint) and no variant of it; every other limited endpoint returns 503 with message 'That is unavailable right now. Try again in a few minutes.'; GET /health/ready returns 503 with body checks.redis = 'unreachable' within READINESS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (3 s); the Redis client carries explicit connect and command timeouts read from named configuration variables, asserted by rg -n 'socket_connect_timeout|socket_timeout' backend/app returning hits only at the one place the Redis client is constructed, with both names appearing there, so an unreachable node produces a 503 rather than a hung request; the hold path issues zero SQL statements while Redis is unreachable, asserted by a statement-counting SQLAlchemy listener, and rg -n 'FOR UPDATE|with_for_update|advisory_lock|pg_advisory' backend/app/domain/holds/ returns 0 hits, so there is no PostgreSQL fallback for locking; after a Redis restart every live hold is gone and the next confirm on one of them returns 409 HOLD_EXPIRED with message 'The hold on your seats has ended and they have been released. You have not been charged. Choose them again if they are still free.' (P-HLD-14 row 5).
StatusNote: tests/xct/test_s_xct_20.py now exists (2026-11-07), with the client pointed at a dead port: holds 503 with its sentence, confirm 503 with its sentence and the payment count unchanged, GET /api/movies and GET /api/showtimes 200, seatmap 503 with its own sentence, /health/ready 503 with checks.redis unreachable, both timeouts only at main.py's client construction, and no lock fallback in domain/holds. Three clauses fail or are not run: (1) FAILS AS WRITTEN: the hold path issues ONE SQL statement, not zero - the router's signed_in dependency reads the users row before the limiter's Redis call fails; zero needs the limiter before authentication (a design decision) or an amendment. Try again in a few minutes.'; the cells disagree. (3) Container stopped and restarted, then 409 HOLD_EXPIRED: a live drill.

a variable failing its type or bound exits non-zero printing a message containing both the variable name and the bound; the boot validator exposes CROSS_FIELD_CHECKS as an ordered tuple and len() returns exactly 13 - S7.9's own table numbers THIRTEEN checks; the PRD's prose says twelve and is the stale figure, and an implementation built to twelve DROPS THE MAIL-TRANSPORT CHECK, after which receipts fail silently, each entry carrying a name, and five are asserted individually: PAYMENT_SIMULATED_DELAY_MS = 200000 against SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS = 180 is refused by PAYMENT_SIMULATED_DELAY_MS < SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS * 1000 * 0.1 while 1500 is accepted; CURRENCY_MINOR_UNIT_RATIO other than 100 with CURRENCY_CODE = USD exits non-zero; CINEMA_TIMEZONE = Asia/Nowhere exits non-zero while Asia/Kolkata is accepted; COOKIE_SECURE true with PUBLIC_BASE_URL beginning http:// exits non-zero; API_PORT and WORKER_METRICS_PORT set equal, and each set to 80 and to 70000, exit non-zero in both the api and the worker process; the resolved configuration is logged exactly once at boot, asserted by counting lines whose message is 'configuration resolved' and finding 1, with every value whose name matches (SECRET|PASSWORD|TOKEN|URL) rendered as [REDACTED] and PAYMENT_PROVIDER present; rg -nP 'ENVIRONMENT|APP_ENV|is_prod|if .*production' backend/app returns 0 hits; the set of variable names declared in the settings model, together with the seed-only variables of S7.9's third table (SEED_DEFAULT_PASSWORD, SEED_CHANGEOVER_MINUTES, SEED_EMAIL_DOMAIN), which the API must not require and the seed script declares, equals the set of names in .env.example, asserted by a test comparing the two sets and printing the difference; every assignment line in .env.example has a comment line immediately above it, asserted by a test walking the file; the value on the SEED_DEFAULT_PASSWORD line of .env.example is refused by the seed's placeholder check (S-XCT-48) and rg -nP '(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----)' .env.example returns 0 hits; every assignment line in backend/app/core/config.py, which is the Zone B configuration file, likewise has a comment line immediately above it, asserted by the same test walking that file.
