Title: Drain on SIGTERM and release this instance's holds through a Redis registry
AcceptanceCriteria: On SIGTERM the API stops accepting new connections, waits out the deregistration delay so in-flight requests already routed complete, finishes them bounded by SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (20), reads SMEMBERS instance:{instance_id}:holds and runs the compare-and-delete release for each key, then exits - asserted by sending SIGTERM to a running container mid-request and observing that request complete with its normal 201 and EXISTS lock:seat:41:312 return 0 afterwards; each API instance generates its id at boot and adds each granted hold's keys to its own registry set with the same 180-second TTL as the holds, asserted by TTL instance:{instance_id}:holds returning a value between 1 and 180 inclusive - never -1 or -2, which Redis returns for a key with no expiry and for a key that does not exist, and which would let a build that never creates the key pass at all; the registry lives in Redis and not in process memory, asserted by SIGKILLing the container and reading SMEMBERS instance:{old_instance_id}:holds from a second container, which still returns the key; a key whose token no longer matches is a no-op and cannot free another customer's lock, asserted by expiring a hold, re-acquiring it as a second customer, then draining the first instance and observing GET lock:seat:41:312 still return the second customer's token; with the release skipped entirely the seats are unbuyable for at most 180 s, asserted by TTL, and SELECT count(*) FROM booking is unchanged; on SIGTERM the worker stops polling, finishes the message it is handling, completes any outbox relay batch in progress and exits with status 0, asserted by SIGTERM mid-job and observing SELECT status FROM receipt_dispatch for that job reach a terminal value; rg -F 'the ECS stop timeout must exceed the deregistration delay plus SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit, and the same file contains the literal string 'SIGKILL arriving during the drain skips the release'.
StatusNote: Only the deployment-spec ordering clause is tested (test_s_xct_31.py), plus the plain SIGTERM drain in tests/test_shutdown.py. Untested, and needing a live-container drill: SIGTERM mid-hold-request completing 201 with EXISTS lock:seat:41:312 = 0 after; TTL instance:{id}:holds in 1..180; SIGKILL then SMEMBERS from a second container; the token-mismatch no-op after re-acquire; the worker's SIGTERM mid-job reaching a terminal receipt_dispatch status. drill_live.py's sigterm/sigkill stages cover S-SEA-17's share only.

Title: Keep every container stateless
AcceptanceCriteria: Both images run with a read-only root filesystem and serve requests without error, asserted by starting the compose stack with read_only: true on the api and worker services and running both test suites against it; logs go to stdout and no file is written to local disk, asserted by docker diff on each container after a full suite returning no line beginning with A or C outside /tmp and /var/run; a poster upload streams to the object store and never touches the container's disk, asserted by the same docker diff after an upload; the guest's seat selection across the sign-in round trip is readable from the browser's sessionStorage key fr.pending_selection - the one-shot key owned by P-ACC-13, the per-change key fr.selection being E2's - asserted by reading it back and finding its parsed seat ids are exactly C12 and C13, and no server-side row and no Redis key holds it, asserted by SELECT count(*) over every table in the public schema being unchanged across the round trip and by a full SCAN COUNT 1000 of the Redis keyspace before the sign-in and after the return producing the identical key set, with SCAN MATCH '*selection*' returning zero keys at both points; the per-instance hold registry and the rate-limit counters both live in Redis, asserted by SIGKILLing the API container, starting a new one, and finding the user's rate-limit bucket count unchanged and SMEMBERS instance:{old_id}:holds still readable; both images run as a non-root user created in the Dockerfile, asserted by docker run --entrypoint id returning a non-zero uid, and a container asked to bind port 80 exits non-zero at boot; the API listens on API_PORT (default 8000) and rg -F 'API_PORT' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit, the specification naming that number for the target group, the security group ingress rule and the published port; SIGKILL sent to a running container mid-confirm leaves no partial state, asserted as a real signal test against a running stack and not as a unit test: SELECT count(*) FROM booking b LEFT JOIN payment p ON p.id = b.payment_id WHERE p.id IS NULL returns 0, SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=41 AND seat_id=312 returns 0 or 1, and TTL lock:seat:41:312 returns a value between 1 and 180 inclusive - never -1 or -2, which Redis returns for a key with no expiry and for a key that does not exist, and which would let a build that never creates the key pass at all; a replacement container serves the same request with the same Idempotency-Key and returns the identical body.
StatusNote: Only the port-80 boot refusal and the spec are tested. Open, all container-level: the read_only stack running both suites; docker diff with no A/C outside /tmp and /var/run; non-root uid; SIGKILL mid-confirm with no partial state and an identical idempotent replay from a replacement container. Open in a real browser: the fr.pending_selection round trip. The poster upload's no-disk clause is asserted for S-ADM-25 but not here.

AcceptanceCriteria: rg -in 'alembic' backend/app returns 0 hits and rg -n 'upgrade\(' backend/app returns 0 hits - no application code path can apply a migration, not at import, not in a lifespan hook, not behind a flag; the container entrypoint accepts exactly four commands, api, worker, migrate and seed, asserted by invoking it with a fifth and receiving a non-zero exit naming the four, and only migrate runs alembic upgrade head and exits with the migration's status, while api and worker start a long-running process and issue no alembic command, asserted by rg -n 'alembic' over the entrypoint returning hits only inside the migrate branch; starting the image with api against a database one revision behind starts the process, returns 200 from /health/live and /health/ready, and returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR at the first request touching a new column rather than failing at boot, and rg -F 'starts healthy and fails at the first query touching a new column' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit so the runbook names that symptom; every revision file's downgrade body is a single raise NotImplementedError, asserted by a test parsing each file under backend/migrations/versions with ast and finding the downgrade function's body is exactly one Raise node; every revision file matching rg -l 'audit_log|booking_seat' backend/migrations/versions also matches rg -l '# LOCK:' backend/migrations/versions - both scans carry that path, because an rg with no path argument runs from the repository root and this criterion quotes the marker it searches for - the comment naming what is locked and for roughly how long; rg -n 'drop_column|drop_table|alter_column' backend/migrations/versions returns 0 hits, so no revision can break the old code that runs against the new schema during the deploy window; SELECT rolsuper FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user returns false when connected with the local compose stack's DATABASE_URL; rg -F '1 manual snapshot, 2 one-off migrate task, 3 verify the task exited 0, 4 update the service' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit and the same file contains the literal strings 'reversing 2 and 4 runs new code against an old schema' and 'skipping 1 makes 2 unrecoverable after seven days'.

Title: Specify the backup, and rehearse the restore with a recorded outcome
AcceptanceCriteria: docs/30 Deployment/AWS_PREP_QUEUE.md contains a row whose Item cell contains the literal string 'RDS automated backups' and whose Needed by cell reads Phase 2; the Zone C specification that row's Spec cell names exists under docs/30 Deployment/ and contains the literal strings 'retention 7 days', 'point-in-time recovery', 'a backup window outside the cinema's busy period' and 'a manual snapshot before every migration'; the same file contains the literal strings 'a restore creates a new RDS instance with a new endpoint', 'deleting an instance without a final snapshot deletes its automated backups with it', 'a corruption discovered in week three is not recoverable from an automated backup' and 'forever retention and a 7-day backup window are different guarantees'; it contains the literal strings 'Redis is not backed up: it holds locks and cache' and 'S3 posters are not backed up: nothing deletes a poster and a new poster is a new key'; the Phase 7 rehearsal restores to a new instance, points a local application at it by changing DATABASE_URL alone, and confirms a known seeded booking is present and correct - reference K7M2QX9C, rendered FR-K7M2-QX9C, seats C12 and C13, both Premium at 28124 paise each (the seeded base of 24999 at the 1250-basis-point Premium uplift), so the total is exactly 2 * 28124 = 56248 paise - read back with SELECT b.reference, s.row_label, s.seat_number, bs.price_paise FROM booking b JOIN booking_seat bs ON bs.booking_id = b.id JOIN seat s ON s.id = bs.seat_id WHERE b.reference = 'K7M2QX9C'; the rehearsal writes one JSON line carrying operator (read from RESTORE_OPERATOR, which has no default, the run exiting non-zero and naming RESTORE_OPERATOR when it is unset), run_at, restored_instance and the three values read back, because an undated claim that it was run is not evidence.

AcceptanceCriteria: Exactly three long-running application processes exist and no fourth, asserted by parsing docker-compose.yml and finding its services are exactly api, worker, web, postgres, redis and elasticmq, of which api, worker and web are the application's and web serves static files rather than running Node, asserted by rg -n 'node|npm start|vite preview' over the web service's Dockerfile final stage returning 0 hits; the Zone C specification file named in the Spec cell of the docs/30 Deployment/AWS_PREP_QUEUE.md row whose Item cell contains the literal string 'ECS cluster' gives each container an explicit memory limit, asserted by rg -P 'memory\s*[:=]\s*\d+' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returning one line per container, and contains the literal strings 'no container runs unlimited', 'killed by the kernel with no slowdown, no warning and no application log explaining why', 'one process without a limit takes the host down' and 'ECS default deployment configuration deadlocks on one instance with a fixed host port'; the API runs one uvicorn worker per container and the database pool size is set from named configuration rather than defaulted, asserted by rg -n 'pool_size|max_overflow' backend/app/core/db.py returning both sourced from settings, and the specification states the arithmetic against roughly 110 maximum connections on db.t3.micro multiplied across processes; rg -c '^FROM ' backend/Dockerfile and the frontend/src Dockerfile each return 2 or more, and docker image inspect -f '{{.Size}}' on the final backend/app backend/migrations image returns a value under 262144000 bytes (250 MB), against ECR's 500 MB free tier, with the figure written into the specification; a measured figure over its container's limit is reported rather than worked around, asserted by that same specification file carrying one line per over-limit container naming the container, the measured figure in MB, the limit in MB and what it would take to fit, and by it carrying no such line when every measured row is inside its limit.
StatusNote: No test file exists for this story. Open: (1) the six-service compose parse, where profile services (test, migrate, roles_init) make the count ambiguous (open question Q-R3-06 in AMENDMENTS.md); (2) the web Dockerfile final-stage scan; (3) the ECS-cluster spec memory-line census and its four literal strings; (4) the db.t3.micro connection arithmetic; (5) image size under 262144000 bytes; (6) the measured RSS rows under load. Items (3)-(4) are on the AWS side: waits for AWS (on hold by the client).
SourceRef: P-XCT-21 SRC-002 §5.4.1 SRC-002 §13.6 SRC-003 OPEN-PROC-01 FR-ADR-064 E8 S7.12

Title: Introduce no scheduled job of any kind
AcceptanceCriteria: The repository contains no scheduler process, no cron container, no EventBridge rule, no Lambda on a timer and no periodic task inside a process, asserted two ways: parsing docker-compose.yml returns exactly the six services api, worker, web, postgres, redis and elasticmq and no cron or scheduler service, and rg -in 'cron|apscheduler|celery|schedule\(|eventbridge|BackgroundScheduler|repeat_every' backend/app backend/migrations frontend/src docker-compose.yml returns hits only on lines that also contain the literal 'no scheduled job'; an abandoned hold becomes available with no process running - with SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS set to 2 for this test and against real Redis, measured in real elapsed time and never with the injected clock, because Redis expires its own keys on its own clock and advancing the application's clock leaves the key in place: 3 s after the hold, TTL lock:seat:41:312 returns -2 and GET /api/showtimes/41/seatmap reports seat 312 as available, with no cleanup job executed, asserted by the worker's job counter being unchanged; idempotency records are never expired, asserted by rg -in 'DELETE FROM idempotency|EXPIRE idempotency' backend/app backend/migrations returning 0 hits, because a key that expires is a key whose later retry creates a second booking; rg -in 'DELETE FROM' backend/app returns hits only on the seat delete and the manager screen assignment replace of S-XCT-09, so nothing is pruned; stuck outbox rows are relayed by the worker's existing receive loop, asserted by a test that inserts a pending outbox row older than OUTBOX_STALE_SECONDS and observes the next poll relay it with no timer involved, and the seat_locks_held counter is reconciled by a bounded SCAN on that same loop, asserted by rg -n 'scan' backend/app/workers returning hits only inside the receive loop; a stale cache entry is removed by its own TTL, asserted by TTL cache:seatmap:41 returning a value between 1 and 10 inclusive - never -1 or -2, which Redis returns for a key with no expiry and for a key that does not exist, and which would let a build that never creates the key pass at all and, 11 s of real elapsed time later against real Redis, EXISTS cache:seatmap:41 returning 0 with a recording Redis client having captured no DEL for that key.
StatusNote: Not changed 2026-11-07. Only the scheduler-word sweep and the idempotency-not-expired clause are tested. Open: (1) the seat_locks_held bounded-SCAN reconcile on the worker loop does not exist (see S-XCT-27); (2) the compose six-service parse (Q-R3-06: services are api, worker, frontend, postgres, redis, elasticmq plus the profiled migrate and test - frontend, not web); (3) real-Redis 2 s hold expiry with an unchanged worker job counter; (4) the stale-outbox relay test; (5) cache:seatmap TTL 1..10, then EXISTS 0 after 11 s with no DEL. Items (3)-(5) can be built now, but their tests are not written.
SourceRef: P-XCT-22 SRC-003 OPEN-PROC-01 SRC-002 §E E-4 FR-ADR-005 FR-ADR-012

Title: Adopt WCAG 2.2 AA as the target, compute every contrast figure, and record the one deviation
AcceptanceCriteria: Every colour declaration in docs/05 B DesignSystem/tokens.css carries its machine-readable annotation naming what it is and which grounds it may sit on, asserted by running contrast.py against a scratch copy with one annotation removed and observing a non-zero exit naming that token; re-running contrast.py reproduces CONTRAST.md byte for byte, asserted by git diff --exit-code on that file, and rg -nP '\d+(\.\d+)?:1' frontend/src 'docs/03 PRD' returns 0 hits, so no contrast figure anywhere is typed by hand; every pair recorded in CONTRAST.md meets 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text and for non-text interface components, in both themes, asserted by parsing the generated table and failing on any row below its threshold; --fr-focus-ring is recorded in CONTRAST.md at 3:1 or better against every surface token it is annotated to sit on; every interactive element on every route is reachable by keyboard, asserted by a test that walks the document in tab order and finds every element with an onClick handler in the sequence; every input has a non-empty accessible name and every error element carries aria-live="polite" and is referenced by aria-describedby from the input it belongs to, asserted per form; the four seat states are told apart without colour, asserted by their accessible names read back verbatim - 'Row C seat 12, Premium, available', 'Row C seat 12, Premium, sold', 'Row C seat 12, Premium, held by someone else' (a seat another customer holds, in SCR-BRW-03's words) and 'Row C seat 12, Premium, held by you' - and by each cell carrying its distinct mark element, none for available, hatch for sold, bar for held_by_other and tick for held_by_me, with held_by_me the only state carrying a 2px border; the seat map contains exactly one element with tabindex="0", asserted by counting, and Tab from the element before it enters the map once and the next Tab leaves it, never 220 stops; exactly one accessibility deviation is recorded, asserted by rg -c 'DEVIATION:' 'docs/05 B DesignSystem/' 'docs/03 PRD/' frontend/src returning exactly one matching line in total - docs/05 Bible/ is excluded from this scan because this criterion quotes the marker it searches for and a docs-wide run matches its own text - and it is the three-minute hold that cannot be extended, with its mitigation of a limit displayed from the start, a warning at 60 seconds and the selection restored on expiry; rg -in 'conformance statement|accessibility statement|WCAG 2.2 AA compliant|fully accessible' 'docs/05 B DesignSystem/' 'docs/30 Deployment/' frontend/src returns 0 hits - the scan covers the three places a claim would actually be published, and excludes docs/05 Bible/ and docs/03 PRD/, which carry all four phrases as the thing they rule out, the PRD's disclaimer being line-wrapped so that no per-line qualifier can tell it from a claim, because a claim would need testing this project has not done.
StatusNote: Nothing is resolved by the 390x844 overflow screenshots. Open: the contrast.py/CONTRAST.md reproduction, the DEVIATION marker, per-route keyboard reachability, and Tab entering and leaving the seat map in a real browser.

Title: Render the largest hall on a 375-pixel phone, and say who scrolls the map and to where
AcceptanceCriteria: At a 375-pixel-wide viewport the 220-seat hall's seat map renders with --fr-seat-size 24px and --fr-seat-gap 4px, read from the computed style, and is never shrunk to fit, because 24px is the WCAG 2.2 target-size minimum; document.body.scrollWidth is less than or equal to 375 on every route, asserted on each; the map scrolls inside its own container and the visible seat strip is 375 - 32 page gutter (2 x --fr-space-4) - 32 map-field padding (2 x --fr-space-4) - 28 pinned row gutter (--fr-seat-gutter) = 283 px, showing floor((283 + 4) / 28) = 10 of the 20 columns, with total row width 20 * 28 - 4 = 556 px and therefore 556 - 283 = 273 px hidden at any scroll position - each of those four numbers asserted by reading the rendered geometry; on first paint the container's scrollLeft is 0 so seat 1 of every row is visible; when arrow-key focus leaves the visible strip the container scrolls the minimum amount that brings the newly focused seat fully into view, asserted by focusing column 11 from column 10 and observing scrollLeft change by exactly 21 - column 11 occupies x 280-304 against a 283 px strip, so the minimum movement that brings it fully into view is 304-283 = 21, not the 28 px pitch and not by the amount that would centre it, with no transition duration above --fr-motion-base (200ms) and document.body.scrollLeft unchanged; a restored selection scrolls to the first restored seat and a 409 carrying details.unavailable_seats scrolls to the first named seat, both asserted by the same minimum-movement equality; the container's computed scroll-padding-inline-start equals var(--fr-seat-gutter), asserted by reading it, so no focused cell comes to rest under the pinned row gutter, which would be WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11; a poll response leaves scrollLeft unchanged, asserted by reading it before and after; every poster slot's computed aspect-ratio is 2 / 3 and its container's offsetHeight is identical before and after the image loads.
StatusNote: Needs a real browser: every clause is rendered geometry (the 283px strip, scrollLeft +21, scroll-padding, aspect-ratio). The 0px-overflow phone screenshots do not measure these.
SourceRef: P-XCT-25 SRC-001 §6.1 SRC-003 OPEN-SCALE-02 FR-ADR-044 FR-ADR-016 E8 S7.13

day index d = 0..29 maps to a local date offset of d - 15, giving exactly 360 showtimes before today and exactly 360 from today onward, each read back with a SELECT against the injected clock; the placeholder identity is (screen_id, starts_at), and on every run after the first the anchor is the local date of the earliest existing seeded showtime rather than the clock, so a second run recomputes the identical 720, finds every one and inserts nothing - asserted by running the seed twice and observing SELECT count(*) FROM showtime unchanged at 720 and SELECT count(*) FROM showtime WHERE movie_id <> <first run's movie_id> returning 0; format alternates by index within each hall so SELECT format_id, count(*) FROM showtime GROUP BY 1 returns both format rows non-zero; occupancy_percent = 10 + (k mod 9) * 10 and booked_seats = floor(seat_count * occupancy_percent / 100), taken contiguously from row A seat 1 onward, never reaching 0% and never 100%;
